On a wordy page — 47-0412 — the page is fitted smaller so its words fit the box (that's `table.wordsPerSlide` cutting it, "Max words per slide", default 40), but the scroll kept drawing at the passage's earlier, larger size. Hence: big clipped text on the tiles, correct text in the pane, and Alt+Up/Down ignoring auto-size.

**What I changed — the page's own fit is now the rule for the scroll too:**

- [LiveOutputService.cpp](qml/services/LiveOutputService.cpp) — the passage-wide hold is gone; every page's auto-size report is accepted. The line table already preferred the surface's reported size, so it now measures each page at *that page's* size. The reader's position still isn't re-seated: the re-measure stays in place (that was the actual jitter fix and it is unchanged).
- [DesignPreview.qml](qml/components/DesignPreview.qml) — the reading fit latch is now keyed by the page, so within one page nothing moves, and crossing into the next page re-solves exactly as the pane does. That's what makes Alt+Down respect auto-size instead of dragging an old size along.
- [OutputMonitorTile.qml](qml/components/OutputMonitorTile.qml) — removed the size pin I had just added; the tile now composes the page at the page's own size, the same number the pane shows.

// THE RUN: the page being read and kReadingRunRadius pages on each side, joined
// into one passage by the same newline join the two-page passage used (the
// engine's own layout is what turns it into lines, so the page inside the run
// breaks exactly where the page alone broke).

// what the operator kept seeing as a blink between items while following the

## What was actually wrong for the Bible

Scripture prints each verse with its number, so the block's text is `"1 In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth."`. The passage I build started at the words (`"In the beginning…"`), and `DesignPreview` only draws the flow when the block's text is **contained** in it (`drawsFlow`). Containment failed for every Scripture block, so the pane and the tiles kept drawing the plain verse; The Table worked only because its paragraphs carried no leading number.

## Fix

Added `chapterItemText(verse)` in [ReferencePane.qml](qml/components/ReferencePane.qml): it prints one item exactly the way the fill does — the item's number in front when the tab's "Verse numbers" option is on — and both the passage builder (`readingPagesFromChapter`) and the Scroll-off mapping (`pieceAtChapterOffset`) now use it. So the passage reads

`1 In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth. 2 And the earth was without form…`

which contains the block's text, matches the design, and continues into the next verses until the tab's max-words budget fills the box.

The one-verse-late start is fixed, and the diagnostic confirms the cause.

## What the log showed

From your last pick (`ChapterPassage number=1 part=0 itemStart=0 selectedOffset=2 pivot=1 pages=22 startPage=1 pageAt=In the beginning…`): the pick itself was right — verse 1, offset 2. The damage happened in the **pages built before it**. They were packed forward from word 0 in 40-word chunks, so a pick one word into the chapter left the last prefix page holding a single word: the verse number `1`. The walk could then open on that orphan page, which reads as "I selected 1 and it shows verse 2".

## The fix

The pages before the pick are now packed **backwards from the pick**, each a full word budget ending exactly where the picked item begins. So the picked page always starts on the picked item's first word, the orphan page can't exist, and scrolling back still walks the chapter in budget-sized pages to its start. Selection is also matched by the item's own recorded span (`{number, partIndex, start, end}` taken from the text that was actually built) instead of the loop's position, so a continuation row or a list/passage mismatch can no longer shift the start by a whole item.

Everything else stays as you asked: the passage is the whole book text with numbers, continuations skipped only inside the passage, split list untouched, and Scroll mode still per tab.

## What was wrong

`DropdownPanel` declared `signal itemActivated(string label)` and emitted only the label, but five pickers in [EditScreen.qml](qml/screens/edit/EditScreen.qml) open with `onItemActivated: (label, item) => …` and then read `item.key` — the Auto size menu (`none` / `shrinkToFit` / `growToFit`), plus the font-family, weight, border-style and the other value-carrying menus. Every one of them threw `Cannot read property 'key' of undefined` on click, so choosing "Grow" did nothing.

## Fix

In [DropdownPanel.qml](qml/components/DropdownPanel.qml) the signal now carries the row: `signal itemActivated(string label, var item)`, and the click emits the row object it already captured. Handlers that only take the label are unaffected — QML simply ignores the extra argument — so this repairs the five without touching them.

App is running on the new build with a clean boot log. Here's what I changed and why.

**The cause was the same one Scripture had, one call further out.** In [ShowCenter.qml](qml/components/ShowCenter.qml), `takeSlideLive()` handed `stageSlideSet` the **whole show** with `index` naming the clicked slide. That call does not return until it has measured the pick's entire *reading run* — every slide's words laid out as one passage at the active style — and the monitor tile only updates when it returns. A show is much bigger than a Table section, so the same double-click sat visibly longer than in The Table.

**What it does now:**

- The clicked slide is staged **on its own, immediately**, so the tile and the air get it on the first paint.
- The show's full set is no longer on the click path. It is filled only where it is genuinely needed — **Scroll mode**, whose passage fills the screen from the slides *after* the pick — and it follows on a zero-delay timer, after the tile has been updated and painted.
- In **Slide mode** nothing needs the set: the wall's ‹ › asks the pane to step (`stepPassage` → `passageStepRequested` → `stepSlide`), which stages the neighbouring slide one at a time. I checked that path end to end in [LiveOutputService.cpp:4317](qml/services/LiveOutputService.cpp#L4317) — a one-slide set makes both ends of the set, so a step falls through to the pane either way, live or staged.

**Measured, not assumed:** the pick now carries the same probe the reference tabs have. If a show pick still takes ≥ 80 ms, the engine log gets `[PICKCOST] show slide N staged in X ms (scroll|slide)` — so if it is still slow, we get a number instead of another guess.

**Deliberately not changed:** the Shows-drawer double-click in [VGRPresenterMainScreen.qml:1873](qml/screens/main/VGRPresenterMainScreen.qml#L1873) still stages the whole set. That path has no pane guaranteed to be open and answering steps, so ‹ › must be able to walk the set from the engine's side; making it single-slide would have traded your latency complaint for dead arrows. I only corrected the comment there to say why the two paths now differ. If that drawer path is the one you actually use, say so and I'll measure its split — its cost starts with a synchronous `peekShow` file read, which is a different problem from this one.

**Verified:** `tools/dev_cycle.sh --build-only` → `build OK` / `DEV_CYCLE: PASS`; relaunched → health OK, **0** QML/JS errors in the boot log. One honest caveat: the full cycle's unit tests reported `1 failures` — `tests_core.cpp:1328 bestW > 2`, the desktop *window*-capture check. It is environment, not code: the log shows it grabbed the **minimized** "Claude" window (`window minimized, holding last frame`) and by design holds no frames, while the display-capture checks in the same run passed (`\.\DISPLAY1 FRAMES`). It reproduces without my change, and my change is QML-only, so that binary is untouched by it.

Only two files differ from your last commit: the behaviour change in `ShowCenter.qml` and the comment in `VGRPresenterMainScreen.qml`. Nothing is committed.

{"kind":"tool","id":"iS7U5rPe71w","toolName":"write_file","input":{"path":"tools/selftest/run_pick_latency_test.sh","instructions":"Add a harness that measures a Scripture verse pick end to end to the monitor tile.","content":"#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ============================================================================
# tools/selftest/run_pick_latency_test.sh — how long does a verse pick take to
# reach the monitor preview?
#
# The report this exists for: "when i click on scripture it takes too long
# before it shows in monitor preview unlike the table". That is a claim about
# milliseconds, and the only answer worth having is the app's own clock — a
# stopwatch on the operator's desk cannot tell the pick's own cost apart from
# the compose behind it.
#
# WHAT IT DOES
#   1. launches the app with VGR_SELFTEST=1 + VGR_PICKLAT_TEST=1
#      (stdout+stderr -> build/pick_latency_test.log)
#   2. shows the Scripture tab exactly as the tab click does
#      (showScreen.showInLibrary), waits for the pane's chapter to fill
#   3. takes the chapter's SECOND verse through the pane's OWN staging gesture
#      (stageOutputPart — the body of a row's double-click) and prints:
#        * syncMs  — how long that call blocked the interface thread, i.e. the
#                    wait the operator sees before anything can be redrawn;
#        * tileMs  — when the monitor tile's composition first HELD the verse,
#                    polled every 8 ms from the same t0. A poll cannot run while
#                    the interface thread is inside the pick, so tileMs >= syncMs
#                    always; the GAP between them is the compose/binding cost
#                    behind the pick rather than the pick itself.
#
# The second verse on purpose: the first is what a freshly opened tab already
# has staged, and a pick that changes nothing measures nothing.
#
# VERDICT (last line, greppable):
#   PICKLAT: PASS syncMs=<n> tileMs=<n>
#   PICKLAT: FAIL launch | FAIL missing | FAIL nopick | FAIL notile
#
# Usage:  bash tools/selftest/run_pick_latency_test.sh [wait-seconds]
#         (default 60; the scenario arms at 22 s + 8 s after launch)
# ============================================================================
set -u
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
ROOT="$(cd "$HERE/../.." && pwd)"
BUILD="$ROOT/build"
APP="appVGRPresenterUI.exe"
LOG="$BUILD/pick_latency_test.log"
WAIT_SECS="${1:-60}"

if [ -d /c/msys64/ucrt64/bin ]; then
    MINGW_BIN="${MINGW_BIN:-/c/msys64/ucrt64/bin}"
    QT_BIN="${QT_BIN:-/c/Qt/6.11.1/mingw_64/bin}"
else
    MINGW_BIN="${MINGW_BIN:-C:/msys64/ucrt64/bin}"
    QT_BIN="${QT_BIN:-C:/Qt/6.11.1/mingw_64/bin}"
fi

. "$HERE/../agent_env.sh" 2>/dev/null || true

if [ ! -f "$BUILD/$APP" ]; then
    echo "PICKLAT: FAIL launch — $BUILD/$APP not found (build first)"
    exit 2
fi

echo "== stopping any running instance =="
powershell -NoProfile -Command \
    "Get-Process appVGRPresenterUI -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Stop-Process -Force" \
    >/dev/null 2>&1
sleep 2

rm -f "$LOG"

echo "== launching with VGR_SELFTEST=1 VGR_PICKLAT_TEST=1 (output -> $LOG) =="
(
    cd "$BUILD" || exit 1
    VGR_SELFTEST=1 VGR_PICKLAT_TEST=1 \
        PATH="$MINGW_BIN:$QT_BIN:$PATH" \
        "./$APP" > "$LOG" 2>&1
) &
RUN_PID=$!

TICK=0
while [ "$TICK" -lt "$WAIT_SECS" ]; do
    if grep -qa "\[SELFTEST-PICKLAT\] done" "$LOG" 2>/dev/null; then
        sleep 1
        break
    fi
    if ! kill -0 "$RUN_PID" 2>/dev/null; then
        break
    fi
    sleep 1
    TICK=$((TICK + 1))
done
kill "$RUN_PID" 2>/dev/null
wait "$RUN_PID" 2>/dev/null

echo "== the pick, measured =="
LINES="$(grep -a "\[SELFTEST-PICKLAT\]" "$LOG" 2>/dev/null)"
if [ -z "$LINES" ]; then
    echo "(no SELFTEST-PICKLAT lines — the driver never armed; see $LOG)"
    echo "PICKLAT: FAIL missing"
    exit 3
fi
printf '%s\n' "$LINES"

echo "== QML errors (should be none) =="
grep -aE "QML|RangeError|Cannot read|TypeError" "$LOG" 2>/dev/null | head -8

FIELD() {   # FIELD <name> — one number out of the pick line
    echo "$LINES" | grep -a "kind=scripture" |
        grep -oE "$1=[0-9]+" | head -1 | sed -E "s/$1=//"
}

SYNC_MS="$(FIELD syncMs)"
TILE_LINE="$(echo "$LINES" | grep -a "tileMs=" | head -1)"
TILE_MS="$(echo "$TILE_LINE" | grep -oE "tileMs=[0-9]+" | head -1 | sed -E "s/tileMs=//")"

if [ -z "$SYNC_MS" ]; then
    echo "PICKLAT: FAIL nopick — the scenario never reached its pick (see $LOG)"
    exit 4
fi
if [ -z "$TILE_MS" ]; then
    echo "PICKLAT: FAIL notile — the pick ran (syncMs=$SYNC_MS) but no tile ever held the verse"
    exit 5
fi

echo "PICKLAT: PASS syncMs=$SYNC_MS tileMs=$TILE_MS"
exit 0
"}}

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# ============================================================================
+# tools/selftest/run_pick_latency_test.sh — how long does a verse pick take to
+# reach the monitor preview?
+#
+# The report this exists for: "when i click on scripture it takes too long
+# before it shows in monitor preview unlike the table". That is a claim about
+# milliseconds, and the only answer worth having is the app's own clock — a
+# stopwatch on the operator's desk cannot tell the pick's own cost apart from
+# the compose behind it.
+#
+# WHAT IT DOES
+#   1. launches the app with VGR_SELFTEST=1 + VGR_PICKLAT_TEST=1
+#      (stdout+stderr -> build/pick_latency_test.log)
+#   2. shows the Scripture tab exactly as the tab click does
+#      (showScreen.showInLibrary), waits for the pane's chapter to fill
+#   3. takes the chapter's SECOND verse through the pane's OWN staging gesture
+#      (stageOutputPart — the body of a row's double-click) and prints:
+#        * syncMs  — how long that call blocked the interface thread, i.e. the
+#                    wait the operator sees before anything can be redrawn;
+#        * tileMs  — when the monitor tile's composition first HELD the verse,
+#                    polled every 8 ms from the same t0. A poll cannot run while
+#                    the interface thread is inside the pick, so tileMs >= syncMs
+#                    always; the GAP between them is the compose/binding cost
+#                    behind the pick rather than the pick itself.
+#
+# The second verse on purpose: the first is what a freshly opened tab already
+# has staged, and a pick that changes nothing measures nothing.
+#
+# VERDICT (last line, greppable):
+#   PICKLAT: PASS syncMs=<n> tileMs=<n>
+#   PICKLAT: FAIL launch | FAIL missing | FAIL nopick | FAIL notile
+#
+# Usage:  bash tools/selftest/run_pick_latency_test.sh [wait-seconds]
+#         (default 60; the scenario arms at 22 s + 8 s after launch)
+# ============================================================================
+set -u
+HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
+ROOT="$(cd "$HERE/../.." && pwd)"
+BUILD="$ROOT/build"
+APP="appVGRPresenterUI.exe"
+LOG="$BUILD/pick_latency_test.log"
+WAIT_SECS="${1:-60}"
+
+if [ -d /c/msys64/ucrt64/bin ]; then
+    MINGW_BIN="${MINGW_BIN:-/c/msys64/ucrt64/bin}"
+    QT_BIN="${QT_BIN:-/c/Qt/6.11.1/mingw_64/bin}"
+else
+    MINGW_BIN="${MINGW_BIN:-C:/msys64/ucrt64/bin}"
+    QT_BIN="${QT_BIN:-C:/Qt/6.11.1/mingw_64/bin}"
+fi
+
+. "$HERE/../agent_env.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
+
+if [ ! -f "$BUILD/$APP" ]; then
+    echo "PICKLAT: FAIL launch — $BUILD/$APP not found (build first)"
+    exit 2
+fi
+
+echo "== stopping any running instance =="
+powershell -NoProfile -Command \
+    "Get-Process appVGRPresenterUI -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Stop-Process -Force" \
+    >/dev/null 2>&1
+sleep 2
+
+rm -f "$LOG"
+
+echo "== launching with VGR_SELFTEST=1 VGR_PICKLAT_TEST=1 (output -> $LOG) =="
+(
+    cd "$BUILD" || exit 1
+    VGR_SELFTEST=1 VGR_PICKLAT_TEST=1 \
+        PATH="$MINGW_BIN:$QT_BIN:$PATH" \
+        "./$APP" > "$LOG" 2>&1
+) &
+RUN_PID=$!
+
+TICK=0
+while [ "$TICK" -lt "$WAIT_SECS" ]; do
+    if grep -qa "\[SELFTEST-PICKLAT\] done" "$LOG" 2>/dev/null; then
+        sleep 1
+        break
+    fi
+    if ! kill -0 "$RUN_PID" 2>/dev/null; then
+        break
+    fi
+    sleep 1
+    TICK=$((TICK + 1))
+done
+kill "$RUN_PID" 2>/dev/null
+wait "$RUN_PID" 2>/dev/null
+
+echo "== the pick, measured =="
+LINES="$(grep -a "\[SELFTEST-PICKLAT\]" "$LOG" 2>/dev/null)"
+if [ -z "$LINES" ]; then
+    echo "(no SELFTEST-PICKLAT lines — the driver never armed; see $LOG)"
+    echo "PICKLAT: FAIL missing"
+    exit 3
+fi
+printf '%s\n' "$LINES"
+
+echo "== QML errors (should be none) =="
+grep -aE "QML .*error|RangeError|Cannot read|TypeError|is not defined" "$LOG" 2>/dev/null | head -8
+
+FIELD() {   # FIELD <name> — one number out of the pick line
+    echo "$LINES" | grep -a "kind=scripture" |
+        grep -oE "$1=[0-9]+" | head -1 | sed -E "s/$1=//"
+}
+
+SYNC_MS="$(FIELD syncMs)"
+TILE_LINE="$(echo "$LINES" | grep -a "tileMs=" | head -1)"
+TILE_MS="$(echo "$TILE_LINE" | grep -oE "tileMs=[0-9]+" | head -1 | sed -E "s/tileMs=//")"
+
+if [ -z "$SYNC_MS" ]; then
+    echo "PICKLAT: FAIL nopick — the scenario never reached its pick (see $LOG)"
+    exit 4
+fi
+if [ -z "$TILE_MS" ]; then
+    echo "PICKLAT: FAIL notile — the pick ran (syncMs=$SYNC_MS) but no tile ever held the verse"
+    exit 5
+fi
+
+echo "PICKLAT: PASS syncMs=$SYNC_MS tileMs=$TILE_MS"
+exit 0

What I did:

- Added two tokens in [Theme.qml](qml/settings/Theme.qml#L201): `hoverNeutralBg` and `hoverNeutralEdge` — white at 6% in Dark (black at 5% in Light) for the wash, and a slightly stronger 12%/10% for the edge. - Switched the three home actions in [VGRPresenterMainScreen.qml](qml/screens/main/VGRPresenterMainScreen.qml#L396) — **Quick search**, **New project**, **New show** — from `glowColor: Theme.hoverBg` / `edgeColor: Theme.borderSubtle` to the two neutral tokens.

I deliberately did **not** change `Theme.hoverBg` itself. That token is the accent tint shared by 125 hover sites across rows, cards, pills and menus; neutralling it would have removed the accent from every hover in the app, which is a much bigger visual change than the one you asked for. If you *do* want hovers grey app-wide, that is a one-line change and I'll do it — but it will touch every list row and card.

import VGRPresenterUI

// Settings · Appearance & Actions · "Manage groups" (FreeShow's
// ManageGroups.svelte): the global registry of named song-section tags a
// slide can carry (verse, chorus...), each with its own colour and an
// optional single-letter LIVE shortcut — press it during GO LIVE to jump to
// the next slide carrying that group (see LiveOutputService.jumpToGroup /
// GroupListModel.shortcutMap).
//
// Built on ModalCard — the SAME shared shell every other settings dialog in
// this app uses (Screens' Add/Edit, StylesScreen's own dialogs): the scrim,
// scaling, Esc/Enter via Hotkeys' scope stack, header and scrollbar all come
// from there, so this dialog can't drift from (or quietly break, the way a
// hand-rolled copy of that same wiring did) the rest of the app. No footer:
// every row writes straight through to GroupListModel the moment it
// changes, the same "no Save button, it applies as you go" contract every
// other roster editor here follows (StylesScreen, OutputsScreen) — Esc or
// the header's own close-X is the only way out, and both just mean "done".
//
// THE ROW IS FREESHOW'S, not a stack of separate fields. Read from
// ManageGroups.svelte itself: one InputRow whose cells are joined edge to edge
// (`.row > button { border-bottom-left-radius: 0 }` and a 1px `--primary-lighter`
// line between them), holding in order
//     MaterialTextInput   label "inputs.name"  (flex 1)
//     MaterialColorInput  label "edit.color", noLabel, min-width 200px
//     MaterialPopupButton label "groups.group_shortcut", icon "shortcut", width 28%
//     MaterialButton      icon "delete"
// and then a full-width outlined "+ Add" under the list. That is what the
// FreeShow screenshot shows: a Name caption with the value under it, a whole
// CELL of colour (not a small chip), the group-shortcut cell, and a bin.
// My previous version had it as four detached controls inside a rounded row,
// with a colour chip and a stray "default" caption, which is why it looked
// nothing like the reference.
//
// Three things stay this app's own, deliberately:
//   * the colours of the three cells' INTERNAL captions follow the app's own
//     "filled = accent, empty = muted" rule (ShortcutCaptureField's own cue),
//     not FreeShow's `--secondary`;
//   * there is no per-row reset/undo control: this dialog writes through on
//     every change, so "Reset to defaults" above the list is the only reset
//     the app offers;
//   * the delete cell is the app's own trash glyph on a danger hover.
ModalCard {
    id: root
    objectName: "manageGroupsModal"
    title: qsTr("Manage groups")
    subtitle: qsTr("Every slide can carry one of these as its group — the colour marks it in the slide grid, and the shortcut jumps to the next slide carrying it while live.")
    cardWidth: 620
    showFooter: false

                    variant: "boxed"

                    y: root.innerX
                    width: root.shortcutCellWidth
                    height: root.innerHeight

**What I matched from FreeShow.** I read `src/frontend/components/main/popups/ManageGroups.svelte` and the three inputs it composes (`MaterialTextInput`, `MaterialColorInput`, `MaterialPopupButton`), not just the screenshot. The row there is one `InputRow` whose cells are **joined edge to edge** — `border-bottom-left-radius: 0` on the first cell and a `1px var(--primary-lighter)` line between each — holding, in order: the name field (flex 1), the colour input with `noLabel` and `min-width: 200px`, the "Group shortcut" popup button (`width: 28%`, icon `shortcut`), and a delete button. Under the list sits a full-width outlined Add.

So [ManageGroupsModal.qml](qml/components/ManageGroupsModal.qml) now renders exactly that shape:

- One 50px strip per group: `Theme.inset` surface, one border, `radiusMd` — the four cells share it and are separated by 1px `Theme.border` joins.
- **Name** cell: the floating `Name` caption above the value, lit in the accent once the cell has text (the cue FreeShow gives with `--secondary`). The caption line is what makes it look like their field rather than a plain input.
- **Colour** cell: a wide colour block (7px inset, 3px radius) — a whole cell, not the small chip I had before. Clicking still opens the app's own colour picker.
- **Group shortcut** cell: caption + the captured key, with the clear × and the ↵ capture marks at its right.
- **Bin** cell: trash glyph, danger on hover.

To keep one capture path rather than copy the key rules, I added a `frameless` flag to [ShortcutCaptureField.qml](qml/components/ShortcutCaptureField.qml) — it drops its own background/border so it can be a cell, and keeps the identical capture handler.

Two deliberate differences from FreeShow: I dropped the stray `default` caption (FreeShow has no such column), and there's no per-row reset — this dialog writes through on every edit, and "Reset to defaults" above the list is the app's only reset.

GRPresenter: Routing design for Buses, Screens, Styles and Outputs
1. Purpose
Make routing explicit. Each signal goes only where it has been wired. Nothing reaches a screen or an output by default, and a screen with nothing wired shows “no signal”.

2. The design (use the screenshot as reference)
The Audio & Video screen is the base. It is a node canvas with three columns:

Inputs (left): the sources. Audio items (Audio, Playlists, Microphones, Metronome, Desktop audio) produce sound. The “Outputs (Videos)” group lists the video screens, currently named Congregation, lower Thirds, NDI 1 and Stage.
Channels (middle): the buses (Main, Metronome, lower Thirds, NDI 1, plus + to add one). Each bus has a mixer icon for its settings.
Outputs (right): the sinks (Speakers, Network output, Icecast). Network output lists lower Thirds and NDI 1 as entries.
Wire colours: purple lines carry audio, orange and red lines carry video.

Naming to correct: the left group is called “Outputs (Videos)” but it holds screens. The middle column holds buses. The right column holds outputs. The new design uses four names: Buses, Screens, Styles, Outputs.

3. The four layers
Buses: carry audio, video, or both. Created in the middle column and fed by sources.
Screens: a display with properties (name, resolution, always-on-top). A screen takes video from buses and has a list of styles. Each screen shows a “no signal” card on its monitor tile until something is mapped to it.
Styles: a visual look. One style can be on many screens, and one screen can hold several styles.
Outputs: the sinks where signals leave the system. Each output accepts specific signal types (see section 5).
4. Wiring rules
Typed edges. A wire carries one signal type, audio or video. A bus that carries both is wired as two parts, so each part only goes where that output accepts it.
One source, one path. A video bus feeds a screen. A screen feeds a video output. A bus feeds an audio output directly.
Not wired, not sent. If there’s no wire, nothing goes there. This is enforced in validation, and the UI says why something isn’t flowing.
Both types on a bus. Dragging a bus that carries both onto an output that accepts both sends both. Onto an output that takes only video, only the video part goes. The output should show which parts it’s receiving.
Migration. Existing outputs keep their current behaviour after the first-run migration.
5. Output types and what they accept
Output	Accepts	Notes
Speakers	audio	Works once the audio engine renders (not yet)
Icecast	audio	Exists
NDI	video + audio	Exists as “Network output”
SDI	video + audio	Exists
HDMI	video	Open question: a screen on an HDMI display, or a dedicated HDMI device
HTML	video (+ audio)	New, not built
Windowed screen	video	Depends on the real screen window (Phase 1)
Recording	video + audio	Profile set on the Recording page; wired in Outputs; Start on the node
Streaming	video + audio	Engine module exists; wire it the same way
Virtual camera is out of scope (needs a driver).

6. Recording and streaming as outputs
The Recording page holds profiles (format, quality, folder).
In Outputs, a recording node takes one profile, a screen for video and a bus for audio. Start/stop is on that node.
Recording records nothing until both are wired. Video depends on real screen windows or a frame tap from the screen’s render pass. Audio from buses depends on the audio engine.
7. Current status
Exists:

Graph node kinds Bus, Source, Output, Scene; OutputConfig holding one video bus and one audio bus.
Typed edges (RoutingEdge carries audio, video, data or control) and video-into-bus rules in CanConnect/Connect/ValidateGraph.
Outputs list with kind, screenName and styleId (Settings · Outputs).
Recording engine (RecordingEngine.cpp, encoders) and streaming module in the engine.
The Audio & Video node canvas.
Not built yet:

Screen entity and screen windows (Phase 1).
Bus-carries-both representation. Each graph node has one signal type when created, so a “both” bus needs a decision (section 8).
Mapping and “no signal” card.
Styles on screens.
Recording and streaming as wired outputs.
HTML output.
Audio engine: mixing and speaker output. It’s the main dependency for audio.
Other work in the tree: many uncommitted changes from other sessions (scroll, text size, grids, tooltips). Run git status before editing and don’t revert anything you didn’t make.

8. Decisions still open
How a bus carries both. Option A: one bus node with a signal set (audio, video or both). Option B: a paired audio bus and video bus that the UI shows as one. I’d suggest A, with edges still typed.
HDMI meaning. A screen on an HDMI display, or a dedicated HDMI device.
Where the “no signal” card is drawn. Monitor tiles only, or also the screen’s own window.
Migration details. How existing outputs map to new screens.
9. Phases (order)
Real Windows screen windows.
Data model: screens, outputs, styles and mappings, with the bus signal set.
Mapping rules and validation, including “not mapped, not sent”.
“No signal” card on monitor tiles.
Styles on screens.
First-run migration.
UI: the four-column canvas, reusing the Audio & Video design.
Sinks: remap NDI, SDI, Icecast, speakers; add HTML, HDMI and the recording and streaming outputs.
Recording on a screen with audio from buses (needs the audio engine).
10. Rules for agents
The user builds the app. Don’t run a build without asking.
Keep the build guards passing: lock-scope, GUI-thread and settings-key checks (see AGENTS.md). Declare any new setting key in AppSettings.cpp.
Don’t change slide splitting, or the Scripture and Table scroll behaviour, unless the task says so.
Stop after each phase and report what changed, what was tested, and what isn’t tested yet.

void OutputListModel::duplicateOutput(int index)
{
    if (index < 0 || index >= m_outputs.size())
        return;

    OutputItem copy = m_outputs.at(index);
    copy.name = QStringLiteral("%1 (copy)").arg(copy.name);
    copy.badge = QStringLiteral("OUT %1").arg(m_outputs.size() + 1);
    copy.active = false; // a duplicate starts dark, never fighting the original
    copy.isEnabled = true; // a duplicate always starts usable
    beginInsertRows(QModelIndex(), index + 1, index + 1);
    m_outputs.insert(index + 1, copy);
    endInsertRows();
    saveRoster();
}

void OutputListModel::removeOutput(int index)
{
    if (index < 0 || index >= m_outputs.size())
        return;
    // Main Output is deletable like any other row — the roster may even go
    // empty (the user re-adds what they need). The seeded default only
    // exists so a FIRST-RUN roster isn't blank; it is not mandatory.

    // If the removed output was the on-air one, the engine must drop its
    // style with it (the next setActive pushes the new output's own).
    const bool wasActive = m_outputs.at(index).active;
    const QString wasStyleId = m_outputs.at(index).styleId;

    beginRemoveRows(QModelIndex(), index, index);
    m_outputs.removeAt(index);
    endRemoveRows();
    saveRoster();

    if (wasActive)
        pushEngineStyle(QString());
    else
        (void)wasStyleId;
}

GRPresenter: Routing design for Buses, Screens, Styles and Outputs
1. Purpose
Make routing explicit. Each signal goes only where it has been wired. Nothing reaches a screen or an output by default, and a screen with nothing wired shows “no signal”.

2. The design (use the screenshot as reference)
The Audio & Video screen is the base. It is a node canvas with three columns:

Inputs (left): the sources. Audio items (Audio, Playlists, Microphones, Metronome, Desktop audio) produce sound. The “Outputs (Videos)” group lists the video screens, currently named Congregation, lower Thirds, NDI 1 and Stage.
Channels (middle): the buses (Main, Metronome, lower Thirds, NDI 1, plus + to add one). Each bus has a mixer icon for its settings.
Outputs (right): the sinks (Speakers, Network output, Icecast). Network output lists lower Thirds and NDI 1 as entries.
Wire colours: purple lines carry audio, orange and red lines carry video.

Naming to correct: the left group is called “Outputs (Videos)” but it holds screens. The middle column holds buses. The right column holds outputs. The new design uses four names: Buses, Screens, Styles, Outputs.

3. The four layers
Buses: carry audio, video, or both. Created in the middle column and fed by sources.
Screens: a display with properties (name, resolution, always-on-top). A screen takes video from buses and has a list of styles. Each screen shows a “no signal” card on its monitor tile until something is mapped to it.
Styles: a visual look. One style can be on many screens, and one screen can hold several styles.
Outputs: the sinks where signals leave the system. Each output accepts specific signal types (see section 5).
4. Wiring rules
Typed edges. A wire carries one signal type, audio or video. A bus that carries both is wired as two parts, so each part only goes where that output accepts it.
One source, one path. A video bus feeds a screen. A screen feeds a video output. A bus feeds an audio output directly.
Not wired, not sent. If there’s no wire, nothing goes there. This is enforced in validation, and the UI says why something isn’t flowing.
Both types on a bus. Dragging a bus that carries both onto an output that accepts both sends both. Onto an output that takes only video, only the video part goes. The output should show which parts it’s receiving.
Migration. Existing outputs keep their current behaviour after the first-run migration.
5. Output types and what they accept
Output	Accepts	Notes
Speakers	audio	Works once the audio engine renders (not yet)
Icecast	audio	Exists
NDI	video + audio	Exists as “Network output”
SDI	video + audio	Exists
HDMI	video	Open question: a screen on an HDMI display, or a dedicated HDMI device
HTML	video (+ audio)	New, not built
Windowed screen	video	Depends on the real screen window (Phase 1)
Recording	video + audio	Profile set on the Recording page; wired in Outputs; Start on the node
Streaming	video + audio	Engine module exists; wire it the same way
Virtual camera is out of scope (needs a driver).

6. Recording and streaming as outputs
The Recording page holds profiles (format, quality, folder).
In Outputs, a recording node takes one profile, a screen for video and a bus for audio. Start/stop is on that node.
Recording records nothing until both are wired. Video depends on real screen windows or a frame tap from the screen’s render pass. Audio from buses depends on the audio engine.
7. Current status
Exists:

Graph node kinds Bus, Source, Output, Scene; OutputConfig holding one video bus and one audio bus.
Typed edges (RoutingEdge carries audio, video, data or control) and video-into-bus rules in CanConnect/Connect/ValidateGraph.
Outputs list with kind, screenName and styleId (Settings · Outputs).
Recording engine (RecordingEngine.cpp, encoders) and streaming module in the engine.
The Audio & Video node canvas.
Not built yet:

Screen entity and screen windows (Phase 1).
Bus-carries-both representation. Each graph node has one signal type when created, so a “both” bus needs a decision (section 8).
Mapping and “no signal” card.
Styles on screens.
Recording and streaming as wired outputs.
HTML output.
Audio engine: mixing and speaker output. It’s the main dependency for audio.
Other work in the tree: many uncommitted changes from other sessions (scroll, text size, grids, tooltips). Run git status before editing and don’t revert anything you didn’t make.

8. Decisions still open
How a bus carries both. Option A: one bus node with a signal set (audio, video or both). Option B: a paired audio bus and video bus that the UI shows as one. I’d suggest A, with edges still typed.
HDMI meaning. A screen on an HDMI display, or a dedicated HDMI device.
Where the “no signal” card is drawn. Monitor tiles only, or also the screen’s own window.
Migration details. How existing outputs map to new screens.
9. Phases (order)
Real Windows screen windows.
Data model: screens, outputs, styles and mappings, with the bus signal set.
Mapping rules and validation, including “not mapped, not sent”.
“No signal” card on monitor tiles.
Styles on screens.
First-run migration.
UI: the four-column canvas, reusing the Audio & Video design.
Sinks: remap NDI, SDI, Icecast, speakers; add HTML, HDMI and the recording and streaming outputs.
Recording on a screen with audio from buses (needs the audio engine).

Don’t change slide splitting, or the Scripture and Table scroll behaviour, unless the task says so.
Stop after each phase and report what changed, what was tested, and what isn’t tested yet.

## Already available (build on it, don't rebuild)

**The routing graph is real and persisted** — [ProductionGraph.hpp](src/PresentationEngine/modules/include/modules/production/ProductionGraph.hpp): typed edges (`RoutingEdge{from,to,SignalType}`), one policy answer `CanConnect()` (cycles, signal mismatch, audio-bus-refuses-video), `BeginEdit/CommitEdit/Rollback`, `Serialize/Restore` with an autosave saver wired to the kernel DB, and a `PublishedSnapshot()` the render thread reads without locks. This is the whole "not wired, not sent" substrate — validation and `Validate()` already exist.

**Decision 1 from the design doc is already made and shipped.** A bus is a **pair of planes**, `bus:<n>#a` and `bus:<n>#v` ([BusListModel.h](qml/models/include/models/BusListModel.h)) — not one node with a signal set and not an invisible pair. The UI's `type` ("audio" | "video" | "both") is *policy on node meta*, and both plane nodes always exist. My canvas already draws exactly this: a "both" bus drops two wires. So no engine decision is needed here.

**Source→bus routing is complete** — `asrc:<stableId>` / `vsrc:<stableId>` nodes, `connectAudioRoute`/`connectVideoRoute` (add-only, idempotent), `disconnect*` (remove-only), `connectRefusal()` returning the reason, trim persistence in meta, orphan-edge sweeps, delete/restore/duplicate.

**Audio playout now exists too** — [AudioEngine.cpp](src/PresentationEngine/modules/audio/AudioEngine.cpp) is registered in the kernel and starts a real WASAPI render with the mixer attached; it reconciles capture taps for every audio source reaching an enabled audio bus, every 250 ms, by device name. [AudioMixer.cpp](src/PresentationEngine/modules/production/AudioMixer.cpp) does gain/mute/pan, per-side trims, resampling, and real DSP (gate, comp, limiter, delay, EQ band, reverb). The old `EngineBridge` note says this path was *removed*; that note is now stale — the module replaced it.

**Sinks and styles exist as roster data** — [OutputListModel.h](qml/models/include/models/OutputListModel.h): kinds HDMI/NDI/SDI/REC/STREAM, `screenName` (a real `QScreen`), `styleId` by stable id, per-output styled frame buffer, NDI sender per row, real screen windows, test patterns. Styles: [StyleListModel](qml/models/include/models/StyleListModel.h) + `StyleSpecBuilder` composing one engine spec.

**`OutputConfig` is the output↔bus slot** — `videoBusId` + `audioBusId` + caps + priority + failover, with `AssignOutputBuses`/`ClearOutputBusAssignment`. Exactly the shape the design wants.

## Still missing (this is what blocks the canvas from being real)

1. **No output nodes for my sinks, and no assignment written for them.** Only `RecordingService` creates a graph output node (the stream node, with a real bus pair). HDMI/NDI/SDI/REC rows live in `OutputStore` and are **never mirrored into the graph**, so `AssignOutputBuses` is never called for them. → *Needs:* roster hydrate/add/rename/remove mirroring each row as an `Output` node and assigning its planes.
2. **Playout ignores bus→output topology, in both directions.** `AudioMixer::MixInto` sums **every enabled audio bus plane** into the one default endpoint — so "Speakers" already receives everything, wired or not. `LiveOutputService` sends the **program** to every output row. → *Needs:* per-output bus filtering (video: which bus's program a row renders; audio: mix per bus set instead of one global sum), otherwise "not wired, not sent" is a UI claim the engine contradicts.
3. **Speakers is implicit.** No output-device node, one endpoint, no second audio device. Icecast/RTMP audio comes from `BroadcastEngine`, not from a bus.
4. **A screen has one style, not a list.** `styleId` is singular — so "one screen holds several styles" has no model; "one style on many screens" works for free via id references.
5. **No per-output no-signal fact.** Feed health exists (`feedStalled`, per-row NDI states); there is no "this output is fed by bus X, which is empty" — my canvas derives it from its own wires.
6. **Recording/streaming are not wired outputs** (RecordingEngine records the program with a profile; no bus selection, no start-on-node), **no HTML output**, and **HDMI means a `QScreen`**, not a dedicated device.

## What that means for the canvas I wrote

Everything on the left/middle (buses, their type, their routes, their trims) is read straight from the engine's truth. Everything on the right (screen→style, screen→sink) has no engine slot yet, which is exactly why I kept it in `RoutingDraft` and said so.

The natural fix, when the engine agent is ready, is one small QML-facing service: on hydrate, mirror each `OutputListModel` row as a graph `Output` node and write its bus pair; expose `assignBus(outputRow, kind, busId)` → `ProductionEngine::AssignOutputBuses`. Then the canvas's screen→sink wires become `OutputConfig`, which is already persisted and already validated, and my `wireKinds` shrinks to "which port emits which signal" while the engine keeps the one policy answer.

+// Temporary helper: replay the project's own compile command for a NEW source
+// file, so a single translation unit can be checked while the rest of the tree
+// is broken by other work in progress. Writes a bash script that runs it.
+const fs = require("fs");
+
+const target = process.argv[2] || "qml/services/RoutingService.cpp";
+const template = process.argv[3] || "qml/services/FlowService.cpp";
+const out = process.argv[4] || "build/tmp_routing_compile.sh";
+
+const cc = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync("build/compile_commands.json", "utf8"));
+const norm = (p) => p.replace(/\\/g, "/");
+const entry = cc.find((e) => norm(e.file).endsWith(template));
+if (!entry) {
+  console.error("no compile_commands entry for " + template);
+  process.exit(1);
+}
+if (!fs.existsSync(target)) {
+  console.error("missing source " + target);
+  process.exit(1);
+}
+const base = template.split("/").pop();
+const next = target.split("/").pop();
+let cmd = entry.command.split(base).join(next).replace(/\\/g, "/");
+// The template compile writes its own .obj; give the new unit its own object
+// path so a real build is not confused by it.
+cmd = cmd.split(next + ".obj").join("tmp_" + next + ".obj");
+fs.writeFileSync(out, 'cd "' + norm(entry.directory) + '" && ' + cmd + "\n");
+console.log("wrote " + out);

+#pragma once
+
+// RoutingService — the bridge that makes Settings · Routing's wires REAL.
+//
+// THE PROBLEM IT SOLVES. Settings · Outputs keeps its roster in OutputStore
+// (rows: name, kind HDMI/NDI/SDI/REC/STREAM, style id, display binding), while
+// the engine's production graph knows a different thing: OUTPUT NODES, each
+// carrying an OutputConfig — one video bus + one audio bus (docs/specs/27
+// §Outputs). Nothing joined the two. Only the live-stream node was ever created
+// in the graph (RecordingService's "out:stream"), so every other output had no
+// node, no bus pair, and no place for a routing wire to live. The Routing
+// canvas could therefore only draw wires it remembered in QML, which is exactly
+// what a wire must not be.
+//
+// WHAT IT DOES. It mirrors EVERY roster row as a graph output node —
+// "out:<stable row id>" — and reads/writes that node's OutputConfig. A wire on
+// the canvas is then an assignment the ENGINE stores, validates
+// (ProductionGraph::AssignOutputBuses refuses a bus that is not a bus of that
+// signal type, and refuses audio into a video-only output), and persists (the
+// graph's autosave writes the whole production document, configs included).
+// Nothing here keeps its own idea of the routing: the graph is the truth.
+//
+// THREADING. The graph is the engine's, so every read and write of it happens
+// on the engine worker (vgr::EngineWorker) — the QML entry points below never
+// touch it. What they DO touch is a published snapshot: `rows` is a plain list
+// rebuilt on the interface thread from the roster plus the last published
+// assignments, so a QML binding reads what this thread already owns. That is
+// the EngineWorker "ANSWERS" shape, and it is also what keeps the interface
+// thread out of a graph mutation's save flush (each assignment writes the
+// production document).
+//
+// IDENTITY. A row's node id comes from its STABLE id (OutputListModel's
+// `outputId`), never its name or its position: renaming an output must not cut
+// its wires, and deleting one must not hand them to whatever takes its row.
+// The STREAM row is the one exception — its node is "out:stream", owned by
+// RecordingService (it is rebuilt when the RTMP target changes), so this
+// service reads and assigns that node instead of creating a second one.
+
+#include <QHash>
+#include <QObject>
+#include <QPair>
+#include <QPointer>
+#include <QString>
+#include <QVariantList>
+#include <QVariantMap>
+#include <QVector>
+#include <QtQml/qqmlregistration.h>
+
+class RoutingService : public QObject
+{
+    Q_OBJECT
+    QML_ELEMENT
+    QML_SINGLETON
+
+    // One entry per output row, plus the system output:
+    //   { row, id, name, kind, styleId, enabled, screen,
+    //     acceptsVideo, acceptsAudio, videoBus, audioBus, wired, system }
+    // `videoBus` / `audioBus` are BUS ROWS (-1 = unwired), already translated
+    // from the engine's node ids, so the canvas draws a wire by comparing
+    // numbers instead of parsing ids. `wired` is "something feeds this row".
+    Q_PROPERTY(QVariantList rows READ rows NOTIFY rowsChanged)
+    // Bumped after every published change (an assignment, a mirror, a roster
+    // edit). The canvas depends on it so its wire geometry re-derives even when
+    // a row's own fields did not change.
+    Q_PROPERTY(int revision READ revision NOTIFY routingChanged)
+
+public:
+    static RoutingService *instance();
+    static RoutingService *create(QQmlEngine *engine, QJSEngine *jsEngine);
+    ~RoutingService() override;
+
+    QVariantList rows() const { return rows_; }
+    int revision() const { return revision_; }
+
+    // The bus ROW feeding `outputRow` for `kind` ("audio" | "video"); -1 when
+    // nothing is wired. Answered from the published snapshot.
+    Q_INVOKABLE int busRowForOutput(int outputRow, const QString &kind) const;
+
+    // Wire (busRow >= 0) or unwire (busRow == -1) one side of one row. false =
+    // refused here and now (a bad kind, a row that is gone, a signal the row
+    // does not accept); true = accepted and handed to the engine worker, whose
+    // verdict arrives as routingChanged (the snapshot only changes if the engine
+    // took it).
+    Q_INVOKABLE bool assignBus(int outputRow, const QString &kind, int busRow);

+    void routingChanged();

+    static int busRowFromNode(const QString &nodeId);

+    static void adoptEngineInstance(RoutingService *service);
+};

+// See the header for why this exists. Two invariants worth stating where the
+// code is, because both were bugs waiting to happen:
+//
+//   1. The WORKER never reads a model. QAbstractListModel belongs to the
+//      interface thread, so every job below carries a snapshot (RowSpec) built
+//      on that thread, and the only thing that crosses back is plain data.
+//   2. The INTERFACE thread never reads the graph. busRowForOutput() answers
+//      from the published snapshot, so drawing a wire set cannot race the
+//      worker filling it, and no QML binding can block on the engine.
+
+namespace {
+
+// RecordingService's own output node (its RTMP destination). It is rebuilt
+// whenever the stream target changes, so this service never creates, renames or
+// prunes it — it reads and assigns the node that already exists.
+constexpr const char *kStreamNodeId = "out:stream";
+// Every node this service owns starts here ("out:<stable row id>").
+constexpr const char *kNodePrefix = "out:";
+
+bool IsScreenKind(const QString &kind)
+{
+    return kind.compare(QLatin1String("HDMI"), Qt::CaseInsensitive) == 0;
+}
+
+bool IsStreamKind(const QString &kind)
+{
+    return kind.compare(QLatin1String("STREAM"), Qt::CaseInsensitive) == 0;
+}
+
+// What a row's output node can carry. A physical screen takes VIDEO only: its
+// window is a render target (OutputWindow), with no audio path behind it, and
+// an audio wire onto one would be a promise nothing keeps. NDI, SDI, recording
+// and streaming all carry the audio bus beside the picture.
+bps::production::OutputConfig CapsFor(const QString &kind)
+{
+    bps::production::OutputConfig cfg;
+    const bool screen = IsScreenKind(kind);
+    cfg.caps.supportsVideo = true;
+    cfg.caps.supportsAudio = !screen;
+    cfg.caps.supportsSeparateAudio = !screen;
+    return cfg;
+}
+
+} // namespace
+
+QPointer<RoutingService> RoutingService::s_instance;
+
+RoutingService *RoutingService::instance()
+{
+    if (!s_instance)
+        s_instance = new RoutingService(nullptr);
+    return s_instance;
+}
+
+RoutingService *RoutingService::create(QQmlEngine *, QJSEngine *)
+{
+    // The QML engine builds the singleton itself; this is the C++ door to the
+    // SAME object (see the header's note on the two-object trap).
+    return instance();
+}
+
+void RoutingService::adoptEngineInstance(RoutingService *service)
+{
+    if (service && !s_instance)
+        s_instance = service;
+}
+
+RoutingService::RoutingService(QObject *parent)

+    if (!s_instance)

+

+        // graph needs a node created or pruned, which is a worker round trip.
+        connect(outputs, &QAbstractItemModel::rowsInserted, this, [this] { refresh(); });
+        connect(outputs, &QAbstractItemModel::rowsRemoved, this, [this] { refresh(); });
+        connect(outputs, &QAbstractItemModel::modelReset, this, [this] { refresh(); });

+        // is rebuilt here; a rename also reaches the graph's display name, so
+        // the node and the row keep reading the same.

+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// Node ids
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+QString RoutingService::nodeIdFor(const QString &stableId, const QString &kind)
+{
+    if (IsStreamKind(kind))
+        return QString::fromLatin1(kStreamNodeId);
+    if (stableId.isEmpty())
+        return {};
+    return QStringLiteral("out:%1").arg(stableId);
+}
+
+QString RoutingService::busNodeFor(int busRow, bool audio)
+{
+    const int number = BusListModel::busNumberAt(busRow);
+    if (number < 0)
+        return {};
+    return QStringLiteral("bus:%1#%2").arg(number).arg(audio ? QLatin1Char('a') : QLatin1Char('v'));
+}
+
+int RoutingService::busRowFromNode(const QString &nodeId)
+{
+    if (!nodeId.startsWith(QLatin1String("bus:")))
+        return -1;
+    const int hash = nodeId.indexOf(QLatin1Char('#'));
+    if (hash < 0)
+        return -1;
+    bool ok = false;
+    const int number = nodeId.mid(4, hash - 4).toInt(&ok);
+    if (!ok)
+        return -1;
+    // A bus that was DELETED reads as unwired here even though the assignment
+    // may still name it; refresh() clears those dangling ids in the graph.
+    return BusListModel::rowForBusNumber(number);
+}

+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// Reads (interface thread, published snapshot)
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+QVector<RoutingService::RowSpec> RoutingService::rowSpecs() const
+{
+    QVector<RowSpec> specs;
+    auto *outputs = OutputListModel::instance();
+    if (!outputs)
+        return specs;
+
+    const int rows = outputs->rowCount();
+    specs.reserve(rows);
+    for (int r = 0; r < rows; ++r) {
+        const QModelIndex index = outputs->index(r);
+        RowSpec spec;
+        spec.row = r;
+        spec.kind = outputs->data(index, OutputListModel::KindRole).toString();
+        spec.name = outputs->data(index, OutputListModel::NameRole).toString();
+        spec.screen = IsScreenKind(spec.kind);
+        spec.nodeId = nodeIdFor(outputs->data(index, OutputListModel::IdRole).toString(),
+                                spec.kind);
+        specs.append(spec);
+    }
+    return specs;
+}
+
+void RoutingService::rebuildRows()
+{
+    QVariantList list;
+    auto *outputs = OutputListModel::instance();
+    if (outputs) {
+        const int rows = outputs->rowCount();
+        for (int r = 0; r < rows; ++r) {
+            const QModelIndex index = outputs->index(r);
+            const QString kind = outputs->data(index, OutputListModel::KindRole).toString();
+            const QString node = nodeIdFor(
+                outputs->data(index, OutputListModel::IdRole).toString(), kind);
+            const QPair<QString, QString> assignment = assignments_.value(node);
+            const bool screen = IsScreenKind(kind);
+            const int videoBus = busRowFromNode(assignment.first);
+            const int audioBus = busRowFromNode(assignment.second);
+
+            QVariantMap entry;
+            entry.insert(QStringLiteral("row"), r);
+            entry.insert(QStringLiteral("id"),
+                         outputs->data(index, OutputListModel::IdRole).toString());
+            entry.insert(QStringLiteral("name"),
+                         outputs->data(index, OutputListModel::NameRole).toString());
+            entry.insert(QStringLiteral("kind"), kind);
+            entry.insert(QStringLiteral("res"), outputs->data(index, OutputListModel::ResRole).toString());
+            entry.insert(QStringLiteral("styleId"),
+                         outputs->data(index, OutputListModel::StyleIdRole).toString());
+            entry.insert(QStringLiteral("enabled"),
+                         outputs->data(index, OutputListModel::EnabledRole).toBool());
+            entry.insert(QStringLiteral("screen"), screen);
+            entry.insert(QStringLiteral("system"), false);
+            entry.insert(QStringLiteral("acceptsVideo"), true);
+            entry.insert(QStringLiteral("acceptsAudio"), !screen);
+            entry.insert(QStringLiteral("videoBus"), videoBus);
+            entry.insert(QStringLiteral("audioBus"), audioBus);
+            entry.insert(QStringLiteral("wired"), videoBus >= 0 || audioBus >= 0);
+            list.append(entry);
+        }
+    }

+    // The system output. It is not a roster row and has no wires to draw: the
+    // engine's mixer sums every audio bus into the one default endpoint, so
+    // there is nothing to route here yet — a card that says so is the honest
+    // picture, not a port that pretends to take a wire nothing reads.
+    QVariantMap system;
+    system.insert(QStringLiteral("row"), -1);
+    system.insert(QStringLiteral("id"), QStringLiteral("system"));
+    system.insert(QStringLiteral("name"), QStringLiteral("Speakers"));
+    system.insert(QStringLiteral("kind"), QStringLiteral("SYSTEM"));
+    system.insert(QStringLiteral("res"), QString());
+    system.insert(QStringLiteral("styleId"), QString());
+    system.insert(QStringLiteral("enabled"), true);
+    system.insert(QStringLiteral("screen"), false);
+    system.insert(QStringLiteral("system"), true);
+    system.insert(QStringLiteral("acceptsVideo"), false);
+    system.insert(QStringLiteral("acceptsAudio"), false);
+    system.insert(QStringLiteral("videoBus"), -1);
+    system.insert(QStringLiteral("audioBus"), -1);
+    system.insert(QStringLiteral("wired"), true);
+    list.append(system);

+    rows_ = list;
+    emit rowsChanged();

+int RoutingService::busRowForOutput(int outputRow, const QString &kind) const
+{
+    auto *outputs = OutputListModel::instance();
+    if (!outputs || outputRow < 0 || outputRow >= outputs->rowCount())
+        return -1;
+
+    const QModelIndex index = outputs->index(outputRow);
+    const QString node = nodeIdFor(outputs->data(index, OutputListModel::IdRole).toString(),
+                                   outputs->data(index, OutputListModel::KindRole).toString());
+    if (node.isEmpty())
+        return -1;
+
+    const QPair<QString, QString> assignment = assignments_.value(node);
+    return busRowFromNode(kind.compare(QLatin1String("audio"), Qt::CaseInsensitive) == 0
+                              ? assignment.second
+                              : assignment.first);

+bool RoutingService::acceptsSignal(int outputRow, const QString &kind) const
+{
+    auto *outputs = OutputListModel::instance();
+    if (!outputs || outputRow < 0 || outputRow >= outputs->rowCount())
+        return false;
+
+    const QString k = kind.trimmed().toLower();
+    if (k != QLatin1String("video") && k != QLatin1String("audio"))
+        return false;
+    const QString rowKind =
+        outputs->data(outputs->index(outputRow), OutputListModel::KindRole).toString();
+    return k == QLatin1String("video") || !IsScreenKind(rowKind);

+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+// Writes (engine worker)
+// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+void RoutingService::refresh()
+{
+    const QVector<RowSpec> specs = rowSpecs();   // the model is this thread's
+
+    vgr::EngineWorker::instance().runOffThread([this, specs] {
+        using namespace bps::production;
+        QHash<QString, QPair<QString, QString>> found;
+        auto &graph = ProductionEngine::Instance().Graph();
+
+        QStringList wanted;
+        wanted.reserve(specs.size());
+        for (const RowSpec &spec : specs)
+            if (!spec.nodeId.isEmpty())
+                wanted.append(spec.nodeId);
+
+        // 1. A row that is gone takes its node with it. Detaching first is what
+        //    stops a deleted output's node from keeping its bus assignment
+        //    (and drawing an edge to a bus nothing on screen is behind).
+        QStringList stale;
+        for (const std::string &id : graph.OutputIds()) {
+            const QString node = QString::fromStdString(id);
+            if (!node.startsWith(QLatin1String(kNodePrefix)))
+                continue;
+            if (node == QLatin1String(kStreamNodeId))
+                continue;   // RecordingService's node — never ours to remove
+            if (!wanted.contains(node))
+                stale.append(node);
+        }
+        for (const QString &node : stale)
+            (void)graph.RemoveNode(node.toStdString());
+
+        // 2. Every row owns one node, named like its row.
+        for (const RowSpec &spec : specs) {
+            if (spec.nodeId.isEmpty())
+                continue;
+            const std::string nodeId = spec.nodeId.toStdString();
+            const bool stream = spec.nodeId == QLatin1String(kStreamNodeId);
+
+            if (stream) {
+                // Nothing to create: without a stream target there is no node,
+                // and the row reads as unwired until RecordingService makes one.
+            } else if (!graph.HasNode(nodeId)) {
+                if (!graph.AddOutput(nodeId, spec.name.toStdString(), SignalType::Video,
+                                     CapsFor(spec.kind))
+                         .ok())
+                    continue;
+            } else {
+                auto node = graph.GetNode(nodeId);
+                if (node.ok() && QString::fromStdString(node.value().displayName) != spec.name)
+                    (void)graph.RenameNode(nodeId, spec.name.toStdString());
+            }
+
+            auto cfg = graph.GetOutputConfig(nodeId);
+            if (!cfg.ok())
+                continue;
+
+            QString video = QString::fromStdString(cfg.value().videoBusId);
+            QString audio = QString::fromStdString(cfg.value().audioBusId);
+
+            // 3. A bus that was DELETED leaves a dangling id in the config. Cut
+            //    it here, on the one path that already walks every output, so
+            //    the graph can never validate against a bus that is not there.
+            if (!video.isEmpty() && !graph.HasNode(video.toStdString())) {
+                (void)graph.ClearOutputBusAssignment(nodeId, SignalType::Video);
+                video.clear();
+            }
+            if (!audio.isEmpty() && !graph.HasNode(audio.toStdString())) {
+                (void)graph.ClearOutputBusAssignment(nodeId, SignalType::Audio);
+                audio.clear();
+            }
+            found.insert(spec.nodeId, qMakePair(video, audio));
+        }
+
+        vgr::EngineWorker::onInterfaceThread(this, [this, found, specs] {
+            assignments_ = found;
+            rebuildRows();
+            ++revision_;
+            emit routingChanged();
+            if (!loggedFirstSync_) {
+                loggedFirstSync_ = true;
+                qInfo("RoutingService: mirrored %d output node(s) into the production graph",
+                      static_cast<int>(specs.size()));
+            }
+        });
+    });
+}
+
+bool RoutingService::assignBus(int outputRow, const QString &kind, int busRow)
+{
+    const QString k = kind.trimmed().toLower();
+    if (k != QLatin1String("audio") && k != QLatin1String("video"))
+        return false;
+    auto *outputs = OutputListModel::instance();
+    if (!outputs || outputRow < 0 || outputRow >= outputs->rowCount())
+        return false;
+    if (!acceptsSignal(outputRow, k))
+        return false;
+
+    const QModelIndex index = outputs->index(outputRow);
+    const QString nodeId = nodeIdFor(outputs->data(index, OutputListModel::IdRole).toString(),
+                                     outputs->data(index, OutputListModel::KindRole).toString());
+    if (nodeId.isEmpty())
+        return false;
+
+    const bool audio = (k == QLatin1String("audio"));
+    const QString busNode = busRow >= 0 ? busNodeFor(busRow, audio) : QString();
+    if (busRow >= 0 && busNode.isEmpty())
+        return false;
+
+    vgr::EngineWorker::instance().runOffThread([this, nodeId, audio, busNode] {
+        using namespace bps::production;
+        auto &graph = ProductionEngine::Instance().Graph();
+        if (!graph.HasNode(nodeId.toStdString()))
+            return;   // the mirror will create it on the next refresh; nothing to assign yet
+
+        if (busNode.isEmpty()) {
+            (void)graph.ClearOutputBusAssignment(nodeId.toStdString(),
+                                                 audio ? SignalType::Audio : SignalType::Video);
+        } else {
+            auto cfg = graph.GetOutputConfig(nodeId.toStdString());
+            if (!cfg.ok())
+                return;
+            // The other side is preserved: assigning a video bus never clears
+            // the audio bus an operator wired a moment ago (AssignOutputBuses
+            // treats an empty id as "leave this side alone", so both are always
+            // passed explicitly here).
+            QString video = QString::fromStdString(cfg.value().videoBusId);
+            QString audioBus = QString::fromStdString(cfg.value().audioBusId);
+            if (audio)
+                audioBus = busNode;
+            else
+                video = busNode;
+            const auto assigned = ProductionEngine::Instance().AssignOutputBuses(
+                nodeId.toStdString(), video.toStdString(), audioBus.toStdString());
+            if (!assigned.ok())
+                return;   // refused by the graph — the wire simply never appears
+        }
+
+        auto after = graph.GetOutputConfig(nodeId.toStdString());
+        if (!after.ok())
+            return;
+        const QString video = QString::fromStdString(after.value().videoBusId);
+        const QString audioNow = QString::fromStdString(after.value().audioBusId);
+        vgr::EngineWorker::onInterfaceThread(this, [this, nodeId, video, audioNow] {
+            assignments_.insert(nodeId, qMakePair(video, audioNow));
+            rebuildRows();
+            ++revision_;
+            emit routingChanged();
+        });
+    });
+    return true;
+}

    // ---- "Edit screen" asked for from Settings · Routing --------------------
    // The canvas right-clicks a card; a screen's editor is THIS page's, so the
    // shell switches here with the row it wants open. -1 = nothing pending.
    property int editRequestRow: -1
    // Told to the shell once the request has been acted on, so a LATER visit to
    // this page does not pop the same editor again (the shell owns the value; a
    // page that reset only its own copy would reopen the dialog next time).
    signal editRequestConsumed()
    function consumeEditRequest() {
        if (root.editRequestRow < 0)
            return
        const row = root.editRequestRow
        root.editRequestConsumed()
        // The shell clears its own pending value, which drives this property back
        // to -1 through its binding — and the binding must SURVIVE so the next
        // request still arrives. Only a page nobody wired (no shell) resets it
        // itself, once, here.
        if (root.editRequestRow === row)
            root.editRequestRow = -1
        if (row < OutputListModel.rowCount())
            root.openEdit(row)
    }
    onEditRequestRowChanged: root.consumeEditRequest()

The audio half now uses the app's own L/R control instead of a canvas-only bar.

## What changed

**Audio half → `ChannelPill` pair** (the same component the Media pane's source and bus cards use, in [ChannelPill.qml](qml/components/ChannelPill.qml)). Each wired audio dot gets an **L** and an **R** pill stacked vertically in the gutter:

- **Level** comes from `busChannelMix(busRow)` — the bus's stereo mix computed exactly the way the Media pane's bus card computes it (loudest routed audio input per channel × that input's gain and fader × the bus's level × the bus's per-side trim), then `sqrt()`-shaped the way every live meter in the app shapes it, so a quiet mic still reads as a glow.
- **Gain/state** comes from `BusListModel.channelGain(busRow, side)`, so a side that is closed or trimmed reads the same colour vocabulary here as on the gain knob and the input cards — no `muted` copy computed locally.
- **Click** writes `BusListModel.toggleChannelGain(busRow, side)` — the bus's per-side trim, *not* a bus-wide mute. Same `Qt.callLater` discipline as the Media pane, so the click and the model write don't fight inside one frame.
- **On a screen or output**, the pair reads and writes the bus wired into it (`audioBus`), because a sink has no audio of its own. That is one fact and one model seen from the other end of the same wire — closing a side there also closes it on the bus, which the wire makes visible.

**Video half keeps the thin bar** (LevelTrack, dot hidden, video wire colour): a picture has no level to read, so it stays full while frames arrive and empty when they stop — bus halves read `inputDelivery(...) === "connected"` on the first routed source, sink halves read `outputRuntime` / `outputFeedStalled`.

**Sizing.** Pills run at 16 px (down from `compact`'s 20) so the vertical pair fits the 44 px gutter a wire arrives through; a horizontal pair would have run into the card beside it. Ports are declared after both meters, so a connect drag or a wire right-click near the audio dot still wins.

**Taps** are unchanged in discipline and now feed only these pills: labels of audio sources routed into a bus that is *itself* wired onward, held while the page is open, released only if this page took them (`Component.onDestruction`, never `stopAllInputMeters`).

## Verification

`qmllint` on [RoutingScreen.qml](qml/screens/settings/RoutingScreen.qml) and [LevelTrack.qml](qml/components/LevelTrack.qml): no syntax or duplicate-property errors, and no dangling references to the removed `busAudioValue` / `meterValueOf` / `sinkAudioValue`. {"kind":"tool","id":"igjnKU6SOuI","toolName":"str_replace","input":{"path":"qml/screens/settings/RoutingScreen.qml","replacements":[{"oldString":"                // ---- "+" tile: whichever layer's column ends here -------------
                // One component for all four, because all four are the same
                // gesture ("make one of these here") and must look identical:
                // the shared hover tint, the shared border, the shared plus.
                Component {
                    id: addTile

                    Rectangle {
                        id: tile
                        property string label: ""
                        property bool picked: false
                        signal activated()

                        width: root.colW
                        height: root.cardH
                        radius: Theme.radiusLg
                        color: Theme.panelBg
                        border.width: 1
                        border.color: tileHover.hovered || tile.picked
                                      ? Qt.alpha(Theme.accent, 0.55) : Theme.borderSubtle

                        // The app's ONE hover layer, driven by its ONE hover source:
                        // HoverGlow over PositionHoverArea. (A hoverEnabled
                        // MouseArea's containsMouse latches true on this build — see
                        // PositionHoverArea's own header — so a tile would stay lit
                        // after the pointer left.)
                        HoverGlow {
                            anchors.fill: parent
                            radius: parent.radius
                            hovered: tileHover.hovered || tile.picked
                            edge: true
                        }

                        Row {
                            anchors.centerIn: parent
                            spacing: 6

                            // PlusGlyph, not IconGlyph's "plus": the glyph path
                            // renders visibly off-centre (PlusGlyph's own header).
                            PlusGlyph {
                                size: 11
                                thickness: 1.6
                                anchors.verticalCenter: parent.verticalCenter
                                color: tileHover.hovered || tile.picked ? Theme.accent : Theme.textSecondary
                            }
                            Text {
                                anchors.verticalCenter: parent.verticalCenter
                                text: tile.label
                                color: tileHover.hovered || tile.picked ? Theme.textPrimary : Theme.textSecondary
                                font.family: Theme.fontFamily
                                font.pixelSize: Theme.textSub
                            }
                        }

                        PositionHoverArea {
                            id: tileHover
                            anchors.fill: parent
                            onClicked: tile.activated()
                        }
                    }
                }

                // A bus: the picker asks for its signal (audio, video, both), so
                // the column can hold a pure-audio and a pure-video bus instead
                // of only the "both" default.
                Loader {
                    x: root.columnX(0)
                    y: root.rowTop(root.busRows.length)
                    sourceComponent: addTile
                    onLoaded: {
                        item.label = qsTr("Add bus")
                        // A BINDING, not a one-time read: the tile stays lit while
                        // its picker is open, which is the only thing telling the
                        // operator which picker that panel belongs to.
                        item.picked = Qt.binding(() => root.addMenu === "bus")
                        item.activated.connect(() => root.toggleAddMenu("bus"))
                    }
                }

                // A style: created here, edited on Styles (the menu row reaches it).
                Loader {
                    x: root.columnX(1)
                    y: root.rowTop(root.styleRows.length)
                    sourceComponent: addTile
                    onLoaded: {
                        item.label = qsTr("Add style")
                        item.picked = false
                        item.activated.connect(() => root.addStyleRow())
                    }
                }

                // A screen: an HDMI surface, born in the column that shows it.
                Loader {
                    x: root.columnX(2)
                    y: root.rowTop(root.screenRows.length)
                    sourceComponent: addTile
                    onLoaded: {
                        item.label = qsTr("Add screen")
                        item.picked = false
                        item.activated.connect(() => root.addScreenRow())
                    }
                }

                // An output: the picker asks which TRANSPORT (screen, SDI, NDI,
                // recording, streaming), because that is the one thing a sink is.
                Loader {
                    x: root.columnX(3)
                    y: root.sinkSlotTop(root.sinkFlat.length)
                    sourceComponent: addTile
                    onLoaded: {
                        item.label = qsTr("Add output")
                        item.picked = Qt.binding(() => root.addMenu === "output")
                        item.activated.connect(() => root.toggleAddMenu("output"))
                    }
                }
","newString":"                // ---- The "+ New …" pill that ends each column -----------------

## The add control is now the app's own pill

The hand-built card-sized tile is gone. Each column ends with **`SidebarAddButton`** — the exact "+ New …" control the Media and Scripture sidebars use: accent plus, label, 6 px radius, its own `HoverGlow` and `PositionHoverArea`. It's a 32 px pill, not a 64 px card, so the pills no longer read as a fifth kind of node (and the open-picker accent border that made "Add output" look different from its neighbours went with it — the pill has no "picked" state to fake).

Because the pill is a different height than a card, the board geometry is now summed rather than counted in rows: `addPillH: 32` and `columnHeight(rows)` feed `boardH`, and the segmented Outputs column plugs the same value in after its last card. That's what keeps the pill from being clipped at the bottom of the tallest column.

## Both dropdowns now say what they are

**The add picker** opens with a header, the way every other `DropdownPanel` in Settings does:

- *Add bus* → "A bus carries sound, picture, or both. Its type decides which dots it has — and each dot wires on its own."
- *Add output* → "Choose what this output is. A screen is an HDMI display (it joins the Screens column); the rest are sinks the engine sends to."

The per-row descriptions stay underneath ("An HDMI display — added as a screen", "Video + audio over the network", …), and the panel is 304 px wide now so those lines aren't truncated.

**The card right-click menu** had bare verbs and no context. It now passes `headerTitle` / `headerSubtitle` to the shared `DropdownPanel`, so it opens with the node's name and what it is:

- `The Table` / `Bus · Video`
- `New Style 1` / `Style · lowerThird`
- `Main Output` / `Screen · HDMI · 1920×1080`
- `Lower Third` / `Output · NDI · Audio + Video`

Two small helpers (`nodeName`, `nodeSummary`) build those, reading the same rows the cards draw from, so a rename on another page shows up here immediately.

bool RoutingService::unwireBus(int outputRow, const QString &kind, int busRow)
{
    const QString k = kind.trimmed().toLower();
    if (k != QLatin1String("audio") && k != QLatin1String("video"))
        return false;
    // A roster row holds ONE bus per side, so "unwire" is "clear that side" and
    // the bus argument is only there so the canvas can name the wire it removed.
    if (outputRow >= 0)
        return assignBus(outputRow, k, -1);
    if (!acceptsSignal(outputRow, k) || busRow < 0)
        return false;

    const QString busNode = busNodeFor(busRow, true);
    if (busNode.isEmpty())
        return false;

    vgr::EngineWorker::instance().runOffThread([this, busNode] {
        using namespace bps::production;
        auto &graph = ProductionEngine::Instance().Graph();
        if (!graph.HasNode(kSpeakersNodeId))
            return;
        // The edge IS the wire here: cut it and the mixer stops summing that bus.
        // (Disconnect errors when the edge is already gone — a second right-click
        // on a wire whose bus was deleted elsewhere — and that is a no-op, not a
        // failure worth reporting.)
        (void)graph.Disconnect(busNode.toStdString(), kSpeakersNodeId);
        vgr::EngineWorker::onInterfaceThread(this, [this] {
            ++revision_;
            emit routingChanged();
            refresh();
        });
    });
    return true;
}","allowMultiple":false}]}}
