I checked the engine before writing, and the check reshaped what the UI needed — here is where it landed.

## What the engine actually offers now (audited, not assumed)

- **Audio is real and rendered**: `AudioEngine` owns `production::AudioMixer`, which sums each audio bus plane from *captured* source taps (`AttachTaps`), applies the bus's per-side trims and processing chain, and publishes `ProgramLevels`. There is no fake waveform anywhere.
- **The speaker endpoint moved into the graph**: `AudioMixer::kSpeakersOutputId = "out:speakers"`, created by `AudioEngine::EnsureSpeakersOutput()`, and — this is the part that mattered — `MixSelected` resolves "which buses feed this output" through **graph edges**, not `OutputConfig`.
- **Recording** has its encoder, a pump, and per-output mix taps (`AddMixTap(outputNodeId, …)`), so a recording hears only what is wired to it.
- **HTML output** exists as `display::HtmlOutputServer` (a browser polls a PNG endpoint backed by the newest frame) but has no service/QML binding yet.
- **Not there yet**: engine-side screen entities/windows (screens are still QML `OutputWindow` bound to a monitor), and the `modules/streaming` folder is just a README.

## The bug that audit exposed, and the fix

The canvas's **Speakers** card said "always on", had no port, and `acceptsAudio: false` — correct for the old mixer, wrong for the new one. Consequences: a bus created after boot could never reach the speakers (only buses present at `EnsureSpeakersOutput` time get auto-connected), and an audio assignment wrote `OutputConfig` only, which the mixer never reads.

[RoutingService.cpp](qml/services/RoutingService.cpp) / [RoutingService.h](qml/services/include/services/RoutingService.h):

- The Speakers row is now a real sink on `out:speakers`: audio-only, never created or pruned by this service (AudioEngine owns the node and its caps).
- Its state is read from **edges** (`graph.Upstream`), so it shows what the mixer is truly summing — including the buses auto-connected at boot, which the old config-only read could not see.
- Wiring adds an edge; `unwireBus(row, kind, bus)` was added because this sink is a **sum** — "clear the audio side" would have removed every bus at once. Roster rows keep one bus per side, so there `unwireBus` is just `assignBus(row, kind, -1)`.
- Roster-row writes now keep the edge in step with the config (`Connect`/`Disconnect`), so a wired video bus is an edge too, and a deleted bus's dangling id has its edge cut as well.
- The row publishes `audioBuses` (a list) alongside `audioBus`; every row publishes it, so the canvas reads one shape.

[RoutingScreen.qml](qml/screens/settings/RoutingScreen.qml):

- Speakers gets its audio dot, its wire, its drop target, and `"audio in"` / `"N buses in"` / `"silent"` instead of "always on"; accent is the audio colour.
- One wire **per feeding bus** on the sum sink (they all land on the one dot — literally one input).
- Its L/R pair reads the loudest side across feeding buses (`pillGain`/`pillLevel`), and toggling a side writes through to every bus behind it (`togglePill`), so the control can't disagree with the meter beside it.
- `busHalfWired` now counts the endpoint, so a bus wired only to the speakers shows its level pair, and `meterTargets` opens taps for it.
- The add-output footnote no longer claims there's nothing to add.

## Also written earlier in this thread (still in the tree)

Bus halves that carry audio from a **video** row were metering silence, because the page only held device taps. It now holds `startStreamMeter` for media/NDI rows of wired audio buses (`streamMeterTargets`, refcounted, released on destruction), and `busChannelMix` mixes those rows' own audio with the same mute/fader/per-side-trim rules the A&V screen uses.

## Checks run, and what I did not do

No build and no lint, as you asked. Verification was static: brace/bracket balance on all three edited files (`unclosed: 0`), every engine call cross-checked against the real headers (`Upstream`, `Connect`/`Disconnect`, `AssignOutputBuses`, `Accepts`/`IsUniversalSink`, `kSpeakersOutputId`), and CMake registration confirmed for the service. The files are untracked (`??`) on `dev` — nothing from other sessions was touched.

Known limit I could not fix from the UI: a node carries **one** signal type, so an audio edge into a video-typed output node (NDI/REC/STREAM) is refused by the graph. The config still records that wire, so audio halves on those rows show as wired but won't reach the sink's tap until the engine decides between a dual-typed output node and one node per signal. Recording/streaming nodes also still have no profile picker + Start on the card, which needs `RecordingEngine`'s profile API surfaced through the bridge.

+bool RoutingService::unwireBus(int outputRow, const QString &kind, int busRow)
+{
+    const QString k = kind.trimmed().toLower();
+    if (k != QLatin1String("audio") && k != QLatin1String("video"))
+        return false;
+    // A roster row holds ONE bus per side, so "unwire" is "clear that side" and
+    // the bus argument is only there so the canvas can name the wire it removed.
+    if (outputRow >= 0)
+        return assignBus(outputRow, k, -1);
+    if (!acceptsSignal(outputRow, k) || busRow < 0)
+        return false;
+
+    const QString busNode = busNodeFor(busRow, true);
+    if (busNode.isEmpty())
+        return false;
+
+    vgr::EngineWorker::instance().runOffThread([this, busNode] {
+        using namespace bps::production;
+        auto &graph = ProductionEngine::Instance().Graph();
+        if (!graph.HasNode(kSpeakersNodeId))
+            return;
+        // The edge IS the wire here: cut it and the mixer stops summing that bus.

+        // on a wire whose bus was deleted elsewhere — and that is a no-op, not a

+        });

// One typed connection point on the Settings · Routing canvas.
//
// The canvas POSITIONS these (it owns the geometry formulas), so a port is a
// bare dot that knows which node and WHICH SIGNAL it belongs to and reports its
// drag in SCENE coordinates — the canvas converts once with mapFromItem(null, …).
// Reporting the dot's own local x/y would fold its hit area's margin into every
// point, which is the bug PortDot.qml's header records from the Audio & Video
// board.
//
// ONE PORT PER SIGNAL, not one per card. A bus that carries both is two dots
// (audio above, video below) and an output that takes both is two dots too, so
// the audio half and the video half of a both-bus are wired — and explained —
// separately. The kind therefore rides WITH the gesture: a drag that starts on
// an audio dot can only ever land on another audio dot.
Rectangle {
    id: root

    // The canvas's key for the node this port belongs to.
    property string nodeKey: ""
    // The signal this dot carries: "audio" | "video" | "style".
    property string kind: ""
    // The signal colour this port carries (audio / video / style).
    property color portColor: Theme.accent
    // Something is wired through this port — it stays lit instead of grey.
    property bool connected: false
    // This port is where the live drag started / where it would land.
    property bool dragOrigin: false
    property bool dragTarget: false

    // handler per port list, so the port — not the delegate — is what says which

    signal dragStarted(string key, string kind, real sceneX, real sceneY)

## 1. The purple footer buttons → a `+` in each column header

    auto pump = std::make_shared<Pump>();
    pump->recordingId = recordingId;
    pump->bufferName = kOnAirBuffer;
    std::string nodeId;
    {
        std::lock_guard<std::recursive_mutex> lock(mutex_);
        auto it = sessions_.find(recordingId);
        if (it == sessions_.end()) return;
        nodeId = it->second.nodeId;
    }
    // A production node may name its own render buffer in its "recordBuffer" meta.
    const auto node = production::ProductionEngine::Instance().Graph().GetNode(nodeId);
    if (node.ok()) {
        const auto meta = node.value().meta.find("recordBuffer");
        if (meta != node.value().meta.end() && !meta->second.empty())
            pump->bufferName = meta->second;
    }
    // Frames already in the buffer belong to before this recording.
    if (auto out = rendering::RenderEngine::Instance().GetOutput(pump->bufferName); out.ok())
        if (auto* fb = dynamic_cast<rendering::FrameBufferOutput*>(out.value().get()))
            pump->lastFrame = fb->FramesReceived();

    // The audio listener copies each rendered chunk; the pump writes it later. Audio is
    // stamped on the mix's sample clock, counted from the moment this recording began.
    // The listener hears only the buses wired to this recording's output node.
    pump->audioOrigin = audio::AudioEngine::Instance().FramesRendered();
    pump->audioTap = audio::AudioEngine::Instance().AddMixTap(
        nodeId,
        [raw = pump.get()](const float* samples, uint32_t frames, uint32_t channels,
                           uint32_t rateHz, uint64_t startFrame) {
            Pump::AudioBlock block;
            block.samples.assign(samples, samples + static_cast<size_t>(frames) * channels);
            block.channels = channels;
            block.rateHz = rateHz;
            const uint64_t fromOrigin = startFrame > raw->audioOrigin ? startFrame - raw->audioOrigin : 0;
            block.timestampMs = rateHz > 0 ? static_cast<double>(fromOrigin) * 1000.0 / rateHz : 0.0;
            std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(raw->audioMutex);
            if (raw->audio.size() >= kMaxQueuedAudioBlocks)
                raw->audio.pop_front();
            raw->audio.push_back(std::move(block));
        });

    pump->thread = std::thread([this, pump]() { PumpLoop(pump); });
    bool attached = false;
    {
        std::lock_guard<std::recursive_mutex> lock(mutex_);
        auto it = sessions_.find(recordingId);
        if (it != sessions_.end()) {
            it->second.pump = pump;
            attached = true;
        }
    }
    // Joined only with the engine lock released: the pump takes that lock to write.
    if (!attached) StopPump(pump);

So respond with an opinion, concretely grounded in the codebase, and note trade-offs and how it would work. No code changes.

Let me ground it: currently
- Settings · Screens (OutputsScreen.qml) already lists every row as a screen, regardless of kind, and its Add dialog has `showType: false` — the kind picker was deliberately removed ("No kind picker: a row on this page is a screen").
- The Routing canvas splits rows into Screens (HDMI) and Outputs (segments: Audio/Network/Physical/Recording/Streaming) using IsScreenKind = kind=="HDMI" in RoutingService.
- Transport is a property of the row: kind HDMI/NDI/SDI/REC/STREAM, onAirOnly flag, styleId, screenName (display binding), boundsLocked, stayOnTop, fullscreenOutput, mediaFit.

So the proposal amounts to: one column or one page of "outputs", each row's editor varies by transport — HDMI shows display binding + fullscreen/always-on-top + bounds; NDI shows sender name + fps + resolution; SDI shows device/res; REC shows profile/destination; STREAM shows target.

This is basically what OutputsScreen already is (a single roster page), and the change would be:
1. Drop the Screens/Outputs split in the Routing canvas → one Outputs column (still segmented by transport for scanning), or drop segmentation too.
2. Make the row editor kind-specific (sections appear per transport) — the "kind" field becomes the thing that selects the form rather than a separate screen concept.
3. Data model: no new fields needed; kind + onAirOnly + screenName already carry it. OutputStore keeps styleId, screenName etc.

Trade-offs / where it gets complex:
- Per-row form variance: the Add dialog and Edit dialog have to branch; today `ScreenForm` already has showType toggle and display placement picker, so the pieces exist. The DPI/fullscreen/lock/stayOnTop choices only make sense for HDMI; NDI needs sender name; REC needs profile + folder; STREAM needs target + bitrate. So the add/edit becomes a small switch, and validation differs (an NDI row cannot be "the active output window").
- "Main Output" concept: the active row (outputs active flag) drives LiveOutputService's screen priority and the on-air style push. With one list, exactly-one-active still needs to hold; that's where most bugs live (activeIndex, isMainOutput, outputsForScreens).
- Routing: `RoutingService` currently treats HDMI as a screen so that style→screen and screen→sink wires exist. If screens disappear, the style wire should land on the row itself (style is already per-output row: OutputListModel.setStyle) — the style→screen wire exists only because screens were a separate column; with one list the style wire attaches directly to whichever output wears the look. Simpler, not more complex. Good argument.
- The screen→sink wire (a screen's picture feeding NDI) disappears as a concept; instead a row's picture is whatever bus it's wired to (which I just implemented). So one column actually REDUCES cases: no screen→sink, only bus→row.
- Audio: HDMI rows today accept video only; NDI/SDI/REC/STREAM accept both. That stays (caps per kind).
- Multi-display: HDMI rows bind to QScreen; the display picker must prevent two HDMI rows binding the same display (already handled via displays()/screenName conflict logic presumably).

Recommendation: yes, do it — it removes a duplicated concept and my new wiring makes it coherent. But sequence it: (1) rename/merge the pages: keep one "Outputs" page whose rows open a transport-specific editor (Screens page becomes Outputs; the add dialog branches), (2) collapse the canvas to Buses | Styles | Outputs with transport segments (this is a small RoutingScreen change: screenRows → all rows in the Outputs column, remove the style→screen special case, style wire lands on any row), (3) keep exactly-one-active + display binding rules in one place.

Risk list: RoutingService's `screen` flag/`linkScreen`, `screenFeeds`, `IsScreenKind`, plus OutputListModel's `isScreenTransport`, `outputsForScreens`, and LiveOutputService's screen-window priority; QML references to `screenRows`.

I think you're right, and it's the smaller design — not the more complex one. Here's my honest read of it.

**Why it simplifies things.** "Screen" was never its own thing in the data: a roster row already carries `kind` (HDMI / NDI / SDI / REC / STREAM), `onAirOnly`, `screenName` (the display binding), `boundsLocked`, `stayOnTop`, `fullscreenOutput`, and `styleId`. The Screens page already lists *every* row and its own Edit dialog literally says *"a row on this page is a screen, the transport behind it is wired on Routing"*. So "Screens" is a second name for the same rows, and having two names is exactly what just bit us in the picker (two screens shown, three in the roster). Your proposal deletes the alias rather than patching around it.

**What collapses**
- One page: Outputs, one roster. Add a row, pick its transport, and the **editor below it changes with the transport** — HDMI gets display picker, fullscreen/always-on-top, bounds lock, test pattern; NDI gets sender name, resolution, fps; SDI gets device + resolution; REC gets profile + destination folder; STREAM gets target + bitrate. `ScreenForm` already has the display-placement picker and a `showType` switch, so the branching surface exists.
- One canvas column: **Buses | Styles | Outputs**, still segmented (Audio, Physical, Network, Recording, Streaming) so "where is the SDI?" is answerable. `screenRows` disappears.
- The **screen→sink wire disappears as a concept too**: a row's picture is whatever bus its video dot is wired to — which is what I just made real in the engine (`BuildBusFeedScene`). Today there are three wire kinds (bus→row, style→row, screen→sink); this makes it two (bus→row, style→row), with the style landing on any row that wears it instead of only on HDMI rows.

**What must not get lost** (this is where the real bugs live, not in the UI):
- **Exactly one active output** drives the on-air style push and the live-loop screen priority. Today that's `activeIndex()` + `outputsForScreens()` + `onAirOnly` transport exclusion. One list makes "two HDMI rows bound to the same display" and "two active rows" easier to create by accident, so those two invariants need one enforcement point (ideally in the model, refusing rather than healing).
- **The HDMI display binding** stays exclusive per `QScreen`; NDI/SDI/REC/STREAM rows must be refused a display, and HDMI rows can't be given a network target.
- **Caps stay per transport** (HDMI = video only, the rest accept audio too) — that's what makes the canvas refuse a wrong wire, and RoutingService already answers it from `kind`.

**Cost, honestly:** ~30 call sites care about the screen/output split (11 in QML via `screenRows`/`screenEditRequested`, 15 in the routing service via `IsScreenKind`/`screenFeeds`/`linkScreen`, 3 in the model). It's a day-ish of careful deletion, mostly mechanical once the single-column canvas is in place — the risk is concentrated in the active-row and display-binding rules, not in the layout.

**Order I'd do it in:** (1) one Outputs page with the transport-driven editor and the two invariants enforced in the model, (2) then collapse the canvas to three columns and land the style wire on any row, (3) finally delete `IsScreenKind`/`screenFeeds`/`linkScreen` and the `screen` flag from `RoutingService`. Doing (2) before (1) would leave wires pointing at a column that no longer exists.

One thing I'd keep from the current design: the transport segments in the Outputs column. Merging the columns shouldn't mean one undifferentiated list — you still look for outputs by transport, not by name.

```cpp
// Listen on one NDI output's own mix. GUI thread: this only registers a listener
// with the mixer (AudioMixer::AddMixTap), which renders that output's mix — the
// sum of the audio buses wired to its node — on the audio render thread.
void LiveOutputService::listenOnNdiOutput(const QString &nodeId, const std::shared_ptr<NdiAudio> &audio)
{
    if (!audio || audio->mixTap != 0 || nodeId.isEmpty())
        return;
    audio->nodeId = nodeId.toStdString();
    // The callback OWNS a reference to the state, so a tap outliving this service
    // (the process is quitting, the engine outlives the UI) writes into its own
    // queue and nobody's freed memory.
    auto state = audio;
    audio->mixTap = bps::audio::AudioEngine::Instance().AddMixTap(
        audio->nodeId,
        [state](const float *samples, uint32_t frames, uint32_t channels,
                uint32_t rateHz, uint64_t startFrame) {
            if (!samples || frames == 0 || channels == 0 || rateHz == 0)
                return;
            std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(state->mutex);
            const uint64_t backlog = uint64_t(rateHz) * kNdiAudioBacklogMs / 1000ull;
            while (!state->queue.empty() && state->queuedFrames + frames > backlog) {
                state->queuedFrames -= state->queue.front().frames;
                state->queue.pop_front();
            }
            NdiAudioBlock block;
            block.samples.assign(samples, samples + static_cast<size_t>(frames) * channels);
            block.frames = frames;
            block.channels = channels;
            block.rateHz = rateHz;
            block.startFrame = startFrame;
            state->queuedFrames += frames;
            state->queue.push_back(std::move(block));
        });
    qInfo(...);
}

{
    if (!audio || audio->mixTap == 0) return;
    // RemoveMixTap takes the tap lock the render thread holds while it calls a
    // tap, so when this returns no callback for it is running.
    bps::audio::AudioEngine::Instance().RemoveMixTap(audio->mixTap);
    audio->mixTap = 0;
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(audio->mutex);
    audio->queue.clear();
    audio->queuedFrames = 0;
}
```

Result<void> WindowsAudio::StartRender(RenderCallback callback, uint32_t deviceId)
{
    if (!callback)
        return Error::Make(Err::InvalidArgument, "Audio", "render callback is empty");
    // Idempotent start: a running stream keeps its mixer (one playout path;
    // a second Start is the UI asking twice, not a new mix).
    if (render_ && render_->running.load())
        return Ok();
    (void)StopRender();   // a dead stream's thread may need joining before reuse

    auto s = std::make_unique<RenderStream>();
    s->callback = std::move(callback);
    s->deviceId = deviceId;
    s->running.store(true);
    s->thread = std::thread([&sref = *s]() { RenderThread(sref); });
    render_ = std::move(s);
    return Ok();
}

Result<void> WindowsAudio::StopRender()
{
    if (!render_)
        return Ok();
    render_->running.store(false);
    if (render_->thread.joinable())
        render_->thread.join();
    render_.reset();
    return Ok();
}

bool WindowsAudio::Rendering() const
{
    return render_ && render_->running.load();
}

#pragma once

// ProductionTypes (docs/specs/27): the canonical Phase 15 model. Production is
// signals moving through a universal node graph — Sources → Processing →
// Virtual Sources → Buses → Processing → Buses → Outputs — for audio, video,
// data and control independently. This header is pure data; the graph logic
// lives in ProductionGraph and the facade in ProductionEngine.

#include <cstdint>
#include <map>
#include <string>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>

namespace bps::production {

// Everything is a signal (docs/specs/27 §Core Model).
enum class SignalType { Audio, Video, Data, Control };

// Universal node kinds (docs/specs/27 §Core Model).
enum class NodeKind {
    Source,
    Processor,
    Bus,
    Mixer,
    Scene,
    Output,
    VirtualSource,
    Data,
    Control,
};

// Bus roles (docs/specs/27 §Bus hierarchy + user brief §3).
enum class BusRole { Source, Group, Program, Monitor, Stream, Recording, Custom };

// Channel layouts — never hard-coded to stereo (user brief §16).
enum class ChannelLayout { Mono, Stereo, Surround21, Surround51, Surround71, Multi };

// Output priorities for safe degradation (user brief §12, §41).
enum class OutputPriority { Critical, High, Medium, Low };

// Scene states (user brief §20).
enum class SceneState { Preview, Program, Standby, Disabled, Emergency };

// Source health (user brief §17).
enum class SourceState { Connected, Stable, Degraded, Disconnected, Failed };

// Processing stages on sources, buses and outputs (user brief §9-§11).
enum class ProcessKind {
    Gate,
    Eq,
    Compressor,
    Limiter,
    ColorCorrect,
    Delay,
    Gain,
    Denoise,
    Custom,
};

// A signal travelling the graph (docs/specs/27 §Clock).
struct SignalInfo {
    SignalType type = SignalType::Audio;
    int64_t timestampMs = 0;   // MasterClock time
    int64_t durationMs = 0;
    std::string format;        // e.g. "PCM16", "RGBA", "H264"
    int sampleRate = 48000;    // audio
    double fps = 0.0;          // video
    int width = 0;             // video
    int height = 0;            // video
};

// Declared resource cost of a node (user brief §14).
struct ResourceCost {
    int gpu = 0;     // 0-100
    int cpu = 0;     // 0-100
    int vramMb = 0;
    int ramMb = 0;

    ResourceCost& operator+=(const ResourceCost& o) {
        gpu += o.gpu;
        cpu += o.cpu;
        vramMb += o.vramMb;
        ramMb += o.ramMb;
        return *this;
    }
    ResourceCost operator+(const ResourceCost& o) const {
        ResourceCost c = *this;
        return c += o;
    }
    int Total() const { return gpu + cpu; }
};

struct ProcessingStage {
    ProcessKind kind = ProcessKind::Gain;
    double amount = 1.0;       // 0..1 intensity (gain dB for Gain, seconds for Delay,
                               // wet mix for a reverb Custom stage)
    std::string custom;        // for ProcessKind::Custom ("reverb")
    // Eq: one parametric (peaking) band per stage; a chain of Eq stages is a chain
    // of bands.
    double freqHz = 1000.0;
    double gainDb = 0.0;
    double q = 0.707;
};

// Volume control on every node (user brief §12).
struct VolumeControl {
    double gainDb = 0.0;
    bool mute = false;
    bool solo = false;
    double pan = 0.0;      // -1..1 (audio)
    double balance = 0.0;  // -1..1 (video)
};

// Meters: Peak/RMS/LUFS/clipping/headroom/channels (user brief §15).
struct MeterLevels {
    double peak = 0.0;    // dBFS
    double rms = 0.0;
    double lufs = 0.0;
    bool clipping = false;
    double headroom = 0.0;
    std::vector<double> channels;
};

struct OutputCapabilities {
    bool supportsVideo = true;
    bool supportsAudio = true;
    bool supportsSeparateAudio = true;
    bool supportsMultipleChannels = false;
};

// An output is a complete signal destination: video bus + audio bus +
// configuration + health + cost (user brief §9, docs/specs/27 §Outputs).
struct OutputConfig {
    std::string videoBusId;
    std::string audioBusId;
    OutputCapabilities caps;
    OutputPriority priority = OutputPriority::Medium;
    std::string group;                    // e.g. "broadcast", "stage"
    std::vector<std::string> failoverOrder;  // output ids to switch to on failure
    std::string encoder;                  // "hardware" | "software"
    std::string networkTarget;            // e.g. "rtmp://...", "srt://..."
};

// Every node in the graph.
struct NodeInfo {
    std::string id;
    NodeKind kind = NodeKind::Source;
    SignalType signalType = SignalType::Audio;
    BusRole role = BusRole::Custom;   // buses (preserved in bus scenes/snapshots)
    std::string displayName;
    bool enabled = true;
    bool active = false;          // in the current program path
    SourceState sourceState = SourceState::Connected;  // sources
    SceneState sceneState = SceneState::Standby;       // scenes
    ChannelLayout layout = ChannelLayout::Stereo;
    VolumeControl volume;
    std::vector<ProcessingStage> processing;
    ResourceCost cost;
    SignalInfo signal;
    std::string fallbackId;       // source fallback (user brief §18)
    // Free-form metadata carried with the node — used by persistence (the
    // serialized graph round-trips it verbatim) and by higher layers that
    // need to hang policy on a node (e.g. the UI's bus "type" routing
    // policy on bus plane pairs). Never interpreted by the graph itself.
    std::map<std::string, std::string, std::less<>> meta;
};

// A named bus scene (user brief §5, §6): switching scenes re-activates the
// saved input set and configuration without rebuilding the bus.
struct BusSnapshot {
    std::string id;
    std::string name;
    BusRole role = BusRole::Group;
    std::vector<std::string> enabledInputs;
    VolumeControl volume;
    std::vector<ProcessingStage> processing;
    std::vector<std::string> outputs;   // outputs fed by this bus
};

// ONE BUS, read the way the Media pane's Inputs tab reads it.
//
// The bus picker and the bus item on the canvas have to say the same thing as
// the card in Media › Inputs — which source feeds the bus, whether its frames
// are really arriving (so a live thumbnail is worth drawing), and the
// three-state light the operator learned there:
//
//   green  "connected"  a source is routed in and its device is there
//   amber  "offline"    routed, but the device it names is gone
//          "starved"    routed and there, but the tap the app holds is handing
//                       nothing over (same amber, different sentence)
//   red    "none"       nothing routed into this bus at all
//
// The rules are copied from MediaLibraryPane's bus card because that card is
// where the operator's model was worked out ("green connect, but the source is
// not active yellow, not connected red"). Pulling the same answers through one
// component is what keeps a future bus surface from disagreeing with the pane —
// and nothing here STARTS work: the routing graph is a model read, reachability
// is a cached-roster probe, and the delivery question reads the taps the app
// already holds.
QtObject {
    id: root

    // Row in BusListModel. -1 = no bus (an unassigned canvas item, a stale id).
    property int busRow: -1

    // ---- SOURCE MODE ------------------------------------------------------
    // A bus is not the only thing these questions are asked about. The "New bus"
    // picker offers the SOURCES a bus could be built from, and a source card has
    // to answer exactly what a bus card answers — is a feed actually flowing, is
    // the device there, what colour is the light — before any bus exists to
    // route it into. Set sourceKind ("video"|"audio") and sourceRow to the
    // roster row and every answer below comes from that row instead of a bus;
    // the defaults ("" / -1) leave the bus behaviour exactly as it was. One
    // component, so a source and a bus can never disagree about a device.
    property string sourceKind: ""
    property int sourceRow: -1
    readonly property bool sourceMode: root.sourceKind !== "" && root.sourceRow >= 0
    // Bumped by the models below; every computed value reads it so a rename, a
    // re-route or a roster change re-answers on its own.
    property int rev: 0

    // The owner's own re-ask (the picker bumps it when it opens, so a picker
    // built at boot cannot greet the operator with the answer it read before a
    // single device was enumerated).
    property int tick: 0

    // The models' own change signals. A QtObject has no default property, so
    // these cannot be child items — they are Connections held by PROPERTIES,
    // the shape DesignBackend/ShowSession already use. The property is what
    // makes the teardown right: a Connections is a QObject owned by this
    // monitor, so it drops its hooks when the monitor is destroyed. A bare
    // `Model.signal.connect(handler)` in Component.onCompleted cannot: the
    // models outlive every monitor, the connection keeps the monitor (and its
    // status probe) alive, and a parked delegate then bumps a dead object for
    // the rest of the session (QML logged "Cannot read property 'rev' of
    // null" for exactly that, on every roster change).
    property Connections busConn: Connections {
        target: BusListModel
        function onDataChanged() { root.bump() }
        function onRowsInserted() { root.bump() }
        function onRowsRemoved() { root.bump() }
        function onModelReset() { root.bump() }
    }

        function onDataChanged() { root.bump() }
        function onRowsInserted() { root.bump() }

```cpp
// THE OTHER END OF A STOP THAT LEFT AN OUTPUT PLAYING. Stop() keeps an output's
// own endpoint (and with it the control thread, the capture bindings and the graph)
// alive while the program is off the air, because that stream can still be heard.
// When the last of those streams closes there is nothing left to hear, so the
// capture devices are released and the control thread winds up — the same tail
// Stop() runs when it finds no output playing.
void AudioEngine::MaybeFinishStop()
{
    {
        const std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(outputAudioMutex_);
        if (!outputStreams_.empty())
            return;      // another output still plays from this engine
    }
    if (programPlaying_.load())
        return;          // the program is playing: the engine's work is unchanged
    {
        const std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(lifecycleMutex_);
        if (!running_.load() || starting_ || stopping_)
            return;      // a Stop()/Start() owns the teardown, or it already ran
        if (controlId_ == std::this_thread::get_id())
            return;      // defensive: the control thread never closes a stream here
        stopping_ = true;
    }
    running_.store(false);
    wake_.notify_all();
    if (control_.joinable())
        control_.join();
    const bool hadBindings = !boundDevice_.empty();
    ReleaseAll();
    mixer_.Attach(nullptr);
    if (hadBindings)
        Logger::Instance().Info("no output is playing; capture released", kModule);
    {
        const std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(lifecycleMutex_);
        controlId_ = std::thread::id{};
        stopping_ = false;
    }
}
```

Done — and no build or launch run, as you asked.

**The gap**

`AudioEngine::Stop()` treated "stop the program" as "shut the engine down": it joined the control thread, called `StopAllOutputAudio()`, `ReleaseAll()` (which closes every capture device) and `mixer_.Attach(nullptr)`. So the moment the program came off the air, an output's own endpoint was torn down with it, its capture was released, and its render callback had no graph to mix from — silence. The PAL already documents the opposite contract for those streams (`WindowsAudio::renderStreams_`: *"their lifetimes follow the ROUTING, not playout"*), so the engine was the half that disagreed.

**What changed**

[AudioEngine.hpp](src/PresentationEngine/modules/include/modules/audio/AudioEngine.hpp) now separates two states: `programPlaying_` (the default endpoint's render stream, or the software clock pacing it) and `running_` (the control loop and capture, alive while *either* the program or any output endpoint is playing).

- [Stop()](src/PresentationEngine/modules/audio/AudioEngine.cpp#L146) stops the program — its render stream and, when it never had a device, the software clock — then asks whether any output stream is still open. If one is, it keeps the control thread, the capture bindings and the mixer's graph attachment, and returns; only when nothing is left does it run the old full teardown.
- [Reconcile()](src/PresentationEngine/modules/audio/AudioEngine.cpp#L470) — the pass that opens capture — now counts a bus as played when the program is on the air, or, with it stopped, when an output endpoint (`StartOutputAudio`) is wired to that bus. That second clause is the one that matters here: with the program down, capture stays open for exactly the buses an output's own device is playing, and it lets go of the rest instead of holding a device for silence.
- [SoftClockLoop](src/PresentationEngine/modules/audio/AudioEngine.cpp#L243) watches `programPlaying_` rather than `running_` — otherwise its `Stop()` join would never return once `running_` was kept alive by an output.
- `Start()` reuses `control_` (`if (!control_.joinable())`) instead of assigning over it; assigning over a joinable `std::thread` terminates the process, and this path is now reachable.
- [MaybeFinishStop()](src/PresentationEngine/modules/audio/AudioEngine.cpp#L352) is the other end: when the last output endpoint closes and the program is already stopped, it winds the control thread up and releases the capture devices, so nothing is left holding a WASAPI client.
- [Shutdown()](src/PresentationEngine/modules/audio/AudioEngine.cpp#L262) is now the single full teardown — it takes down the endpoints `Stop()` deliberately left playing.

**One thing to know about the stopped state:** with the program off the air, NDI/recording/streaming taps get silence too, because the mixer feeds them from the program render (`NotifyTaps` runs inside `Render`). That's pre-existing and unchanged — only per-output devices play while the program is stopped.

**Checks:** `g++ -fsyntax-only` on `AudioEngine.cpp` with the project's recorded flags — clean, exit 0; `tools/check_lock_scope.mjs` — clean, exit 0 (no new lock held across a device or PAL call). Fixed the reverse drag in the wire ghost.

**What was wrong**

The drag ghost's cubic control points were hard-wired to the left-to-right direction:

```qml
control1X: root.dragStartX + draggedWire.bend
control2X: root.dragX - draggedWire.bend
```

So when you pull a wire backwards — from a sink's dot on the right back to a bus on the left, which is how people actually read this board — `dragStartX` is the *right-hand* end, and both handles came out on the wrong side of their own end: `start + bend` pushed the first handle away to the right of the sink, `dragX - bend` pulled the second handle left of the cursor, past it. The curve hooked itself around the pointer instead of trailing it, so the line looked stiff and stopped following the drag. Left-to-right drags were unaffected, which is why it only showed up one way round.

**What changed** ([RoutingScreen.qml](qml/screens/settings/RoutingScreen.qml#L2534))

The ghost is now plotted exactly the way the committed wire layer plots a wire: always left to right, each handle to the outside of its own end. The ends swap when `dragX < dragStartX`, so a reverse drag draws the *same curve the wire will become* rather than a mirrored, collapsing one:

```qml
readonly property bool reversed: root.dragX < root.dragStartX
readonly property real fromX: reversed ? root.dragX : root.dragStartX
readonly property real toX:   reversed ? root.dragStartX : root.dragX
readonly property real bend:  Math.max(24, Math.abs(toX - fromX) * 0.5)
```

It's about which of two pictures a wired output's pass builds. Right now it can only build one.

**The two pictures already in the engine**

*The full-frame bus feed.* [SceneBuilder::BuildBusFeedScene](src/PresentationEngine/modules/presentation/SceneBuilder.cpp#L2593) makes a scene containing one video layer, sized to the whole frame, painted with the bus's current picture (`CompositorState::GetBusFrame`, keyed by the bus's stable number). It's a clean I-MAG of a camera or the Table, nothing else on screen.

*The design's bus window.* A style/slide block of kind `bus` is a live feed drawn *inside the design's own rectangle* — [RecordBusPlanes / RefreshBusPlanes](src/PresentationEngine/modules/presentation/SceneBuilder.cpp#L1400) build that plane while the slide scene is composed. This is the lower-third-with-a-camera-box picture, and it only exists as part of a slide composition, because the rectangle's position and size come from the design's blocks.

**Why it's exclusive today**

[LiveOutputController](src/PresentationEngine/modules/presentation/LiveOutputController.cpp#L1016) decides per output row, per frame:

```cpp
const bool busWired = specs[i].videoBus > 0;
auto sceneId = busWired
    ? pres_->Builder().BuildBusFeedScene(specs[i].videoBus, engine, sceneSize)
    : pres_->Builder().BuildGatedSlideScene(*active, *slide, specs[i], engine, sceneSize);
```

A video wire flips the row to the bus feed and the design is never composed for it — so there is no rectangle to paint into. An unwired row composes the design, and since the wires became the allow-list for bus windows its gate is empty, so it paints no window either. The result of the last change is that *no* output currently shows a design window: an output either sends a clean bus or sends the design with a hole where the window's frame sits. Meanwhile the Edit canvas does draw the window, which is why the preview and the output disagree.

**What the suggestion changes**

Instead of "wired ⇒ throw the design away", a wired row would compose the design *and* fill its bus window with that same bus's live feed — the bus feed scaled into the rectangle instead of the rectangle's frame drawn empty. The two pictures then differ only in framing: full-frame for a clean feed, in-rectangle for the design. Concretely that means the wired row calls `BuildGatedSlideScene` (with its wired bus in `allowedVideoBuses`, so the window is allowed to paint) rather than `BuildBusFeedScene`, and the full-frame feed becomes a per-row choice instead of the forced behaviour of every wired row.

**The trade-off to decide before doing it**

Today's rule is blunt but predictable: wire a camera to an NDI output and NDI carries the camera, full stop. Compose-the-design-instead would send the whole on-air design down that wire, camera in a box — which is right for a venue screen and wrong for a feed you're sending to a video router. So the honest shape of this change is a third state per output ("wire shows: the bus itself / the design with its window"), not a silent swap, and it has to be keyed into the scene id the way the gate already is (`@gb:` in `StyledSceneIdFor`) or the cache will serve a design scene to an output that asked for the clean feed.

---
#pragma once

// THE FAMILY → SLOT TABLE ON THE QML SIDE, and the ONE list of what a style calls
// each content family's gate and template pick.
//
// The engine owns WHICH SLOT a family is (presentation::kFamilySlot* and
// SlideRules::FamilyTemplateSlot — the one place a page's content tag becomes a
// slot); this table delegates to it and adds the only other thing the QML layer
// needs: the property NAMES. Both used to be spelled out in several places — the
// style model's load, save, two setters and its variant map, the output model's
// "familyTemplate" + capitalised-tag concatenation, and the style spec builder's
// per-family reads — so a fifth family, or a renamed property, needed every one
// of them edited in step, and a missed one styled the WRONG family in silence
// (the output model BUILT its key by capitalising the content type, so a tag that
// did not follow that convention named no property at all and the style quietly
// fell back to "the slides' own template governs").
//
// Rows are in SLOT order, which the static_assert below pins to the engine's — a
// loop over this table walks the families exactly as the engine's arrays are
// indexed.

#include "modules/presentation/PresentationTypes.hpp"
#include "modules/presentation/SlideRules.hpp"

#include <QString>

#include <array>
#include <cstddef>

namespace FamilySlots {

struct Family {
    const char *tag;               // the slide's / the tab's content type
    const char *showProperty;      // the style's own gate for it
    const char *templateProperty;  // the style's template pick for it
};

inline constexpr int kCount = static_cast<int>(bps::presentation::kFamilySlotCount);

inline const std::array<Family, static_cast<std::size_t>(kCount)> &Rows()
{
    static const std::array<Family, static_cast<std::size_t>(kCount)> rows{ {
        { "shows",     "showShows",     "familyTemplateShows" },
        { "media",     "showMedia",     "familyTemplateMedia" },
        { "scripture", "showScripture", "familyTemplateScripture" },
        { "table",     "showTable",     "familyTemplateTable" },
    } };
    return rows;
}

// The row order IS the engine's slot order: this keeps the two from drifting.
static_assert(bps::presentation::kFamilySlotShows == 0 && bps::presentation::kFamilySlotMedia == 1
                  && bps::presentation::kFamilySlotScripture == 2 && bps::presentation::kFamilySlotTable == 3
                  && kCount == 4,
              "FamilySlots' rows must be in the engine's family slot order");

// The slot a content type names, or -1 when it names no family: an unknown tag,
// or the Overlays pane's own tag (overlays are not a slide family — the style's
// showOverlay gate is a different axis and is read by name). The MATCHED tag's
// slot comes from the engine, so this table never decides it a second time.
inline int SlotFor(const QString &contentType)
{
    if (contentType.isEmpty())
        return -1;
    const auto &rows = Rows();
    for (int slot = 0; slot < kCount; ++slot) {
        const Family &row = rows[static_cast<std::size_t>(slot)];
        if (contentType == QLatin1String(row.tag))
            return static_cast<int>(bps::presentation::SlideRules::FamilyTemplateSlot(row.tag));
    }
    return -1;
}

// The row for a content type, or nullptr when it names no family.
inline const Family *RowFor(const QString &contentType)
{
    const int slot = SlotFor(contentType);
    return slot < 0 ? nullptr : &Rows()[static_cast<std::size_t>(slot)];
}

} // namespace FamilySlots

Template buses: spec
1. What we are building
A new bus kind, template bus. It is created by picking a template, the one already designed in the Edit canvas’s template tab. Its windows are the bus items placed on that template. A template bus accepts several video inputs and one audio input. Once created, it is an ordinary bus: it appears on the Routing page and can be wired to outputs like any other bus.

Existing buses do not change. A normal video bus still takes one video input and a normal audio bus still takes one audio input.

2. Terms
Template: a design made in the Edit canvas’s template tab. It holds media items, text, and bus items, each placed at a position.
Window: a bus item placed on a template. It is a rectangle in the design that shows a live video feed.
Bus (existing): a normal bus that takes one video input and one audio input.
Template bus (new): a bus created from a template. It takes several video inputs and one audio input.
Output: a destination on the Routing page (HDMI screen, NDI, recording, and so on). It takes a video bus and an audio bus.
3. User flow
Design the template. In Edit, open the template tab. Add items, including bus items, and position them. Each bus item is a window.
Create the template bus. In the bus picker, choose the Template category. Pick a template from the list. A new template bus appears, already knowing its windows from the template.
Route video into it. On the Routing page, drag camera or media sources onto the template bus’s video port. Several can go in.
Route audio into it. Drag one audio source onto its audio port.
Wire it to an output. Drag the template bus’s video port to an output’s video port, and its audio port to the output’s audio port. This works exactly as it does for a normal bus.
On air. The output shows the template’s design, with each window filled by its video feed.
4. Data model
4.1 Bus kind
A bus has a type field. Add a new value, "template".
A template bus stores the id of the template it was created from, in a new meta key templateId.
Windows are not stored on the bus. They are read from the template at render time. This means editing the template updates the bus automatically.
4.2 Windows
A window is a design block of kind bus on the template.
The existing busId meta on a bus block means “this block shows that normal bus”. A window on a template bus does not use busId. It needs its own stable identifier, which is the block’s id within the template. Open: confirm that block ids in the template are stable across edits. If they are not, a new stable window id is needed.
4.3 Routing (graph)
Video edges into a template bus are many-to-one. There is no capacity limit.
Audio edges into a template bus: one only. The second audio edge is refused.
A template bus has one video output side and one audio output side, the same as a normal bus.
Outputs keep their current videoBusId and audioBusId. A template bus fills those slots like any other bus.
5. Rendering
A template bus produces one video frame per tick. That frame is the template design, with each window replaced by its assigned video feed.
The design is composed by the existing scene builder. Windows are painted by the existing bus-plane code, with the source of each plane changed from “a normal bus” to “the feed assigned to this window”.
The audio of a template bus is the single audio input, routed through the normal audio mixer.
Cache keys must include the template id and the set of assigned feeds, so that changing a feed invalidates the cached scene.
6. Required UI
Bus picker (BusSourceModal): add a “Template” category. It lists templates from the template library. Picking one creates a template bus.
Routing page: the template bus is a bus card. Its subtitle shows Template · N in, where N is the number of video inputs. Its video port accepts many wires. Its audio port accepts one.
Edit canvas: no change.
Audio & Video page: no new column. Template buses are created from the bus picker, as the spec above describes.
7. Open questions (must be answered before build)
Which window does each camera fill? Options:
a) You choose a window for each camera when you route it.
b) Cameras fill windows in the order they were routed.
c) Each window has a fixed name, and cameras are matched to names.
What does an empty window show? Options: the design background, blank, or a placeholder.
What happens when the template changes after a template bus is created?
a) Windows added: do they get a slot with no feed? Routing sees the new slot.
b) Windows removed: what happens to the feed that was in them? Is it dropped, or moved?
What happens when a template is deleted while a template bus uses it? Options: refuse the delete, or detach the bus and show a warning.
Audio with several windows. Audio is one input for the whole bus. Does that audio belong to every window, or only to the bus as a whole?
Clean output. Do we still need a “full-frame feed” option that shows one window full-screen? If so, which window?
8. Non-goals
No change to normal buses.
No change to the Edit canvas beyond reading bus items.
No A&V template column.
No HTML output work.
No change to how outputs store their audio.
9. Acceptance tests
Create a template with three bus items. Create a template bus from it. Three windows are visible in the bus’s detail.
Route three video sources into the template bus. All three are accepted. Route a fourth: it is accepted and the rule in open question 1 decides where it goes.
Route two audio sources into the template bus. The second is refused.
Wire the template bus to an output. The output’s frame shows the template design, with each window filled.
Edit the template: move a window. The output updates without recreating the bus.
Delete a source that feeds a window. That window shows its empty state.
Existing normal buses still accept one video input, and their outputs still show the clean full-frame feed.
10. Build and checks
Build and run the app with the repo’s dev cycle script, as AGENTS.md describes.
Run the three repo guards: the lock-scope guard, the interface-thread guard, and the settings-keys guard.

int BusListModel::rowCount(const QModelIndex &parent) const
{
    if (parent.isValid())
        return 0;
    return m_buses.size();
}

QVariant BusListModel::data(const QModelIndex &index, int role) const
{
    if (!index.isValid() || index.row() < 0 || index.row() >= m_buses.size())
        return {};

    const BusItem &item = m_buses.at(index.row());
    switch (role) {
    case NameRole: return item.name;
    case TypeRole: return item.type;
    case LevelRole: return item.level;
    case MutedRole: return item.muted;
    case ChannelGainsRole: {
        QVariantList gains;
        for (qreal g : item.channelGains)
            gains.append(g);
        return gains;
    }
    case RoutedAudioInputsRole: return toVariantList(item.routedAudioInputs);
    case RoutedVideoSourcesRole: return toVariantList(item.routedVideoSources);
    default: return {};
    }
}

QHash<int, QByteArray> BusListModel::roleNames() const
{
    return {
        { NameRole, "name" },
        { TypeRole, "type" },
        { LevelRole, "level" },
        { MutedRole, "muted" },
        { ChannelGainsRole, "channelGains" },
        { RoutedAudioInputsRole, "routedAudioInputs" },
        { RoutedVideoSourcesRole, "routedVideoSources" },
    };
}

void BusListModel::addBus(const QString &name, const QString &type)
{
    const QString trimmed = name.trimmed();
    const int row = m_buses.size();

    beginInsertRows(QModelIndex(), row, row);
    createBusRow(trimmed.isEmpty() ? QStringLiteral("New Bus %1").arg(row + 1) : trimmed,
                 type.isEmpty() ? QStringLiteral("audio") : type, 75, false);
    endInsertRows();
}

void BusListModel::removeBus(int index)
{
    if (index < 0 || index >= m_buses.size())
        return;
    const BusItem item = m_buses.at(index);

    // Engine first: node removal takes its edges with it; the view row goes
    // only when the graph no longer holds the bus.
    {
        GraphEdit edit;
        logIfFailed("RemoveNode(audio)", graph().RemoveNode(item.engineId.toStdString()));
        logIfFailed("RemoveNode(video)", graph().RemoveNode(item.engineIdVideo.toStdString()));
    }
    if (graph().HasNode(item.engineId.toStdString())
        || graph().HasNode(item.engineIdVideo.toStdString())) {
        qWarning() << "BusListModel: removeBus kept the row — the graph still holds it";
        return;
    }

    beginRemoveRows(QModelIndex(), index, index);
    m_buses.removeAt(index);
    endRemoveRows();
}

bool BusListModel::deleteBus(int index)
{
    if (index < 0 || index >= m_buses.size())
        return false;

    // CAPTURE BEFORE THE ROWS GO: the item's own routing lists are ROSTER ROWS,
    // and a row is a position in a list that can move. The node ids behind them
    // are what an edge is really keyed on, so those are what a restore reconnects.
    RemovedBus back;
    back.row = index;
    back.item = m_buses.at(index);
    for (const int row : std::as_const(back.item.routedAudioInputs)) {
        const QString node = audioSourceNodeId(row);
        if (!node.isEmpty())
            back.audioSources.append(node);
    }
    for (const int row : std::as_const(back.item.routedVideoSources)) {
        const QString node = videoSourceNodeId(row);
        if (!node.isEmpty())
            back.videoSources.append(node);
    }

    const int before = m_buses.size();
    removeBus(index);
    if (m_buses.size() == before)
        return false;   // the graph still held it — there is nothing to undo
    m_removedBus = back;

    // The notice is raised HERE, not at each call site: every door onto "delete
    // this bus" (the pane's menu, the board's own Delete, the bus dialog's) then
    // offers the same one click back, and a new door cannot forget to.
    EventBus::instance().notify(tr("\u201c%1\u201d was removed \u2014 Undo puts it back.").arg(back.item.name),
                                QStringLiteral("info"), tr("Buses"),
                                QStringLiteral("ui.buses.removed"), QVariant(),
                                QVariantMap{{ QStringLiteral("id"), QStringLiteral("buses.undoRemove") },
                                            { QStringLiteral("label"), tr("Undo") }});
    return true;
}

QString BusListModel::removedBusName() const

    return m_removedBus.has_value() ? m_removedBus->item.name : QString();
}

bool BusListModel::restoreRemovedBus()
{
    if (!m_removedBus.has_value())
        return false;
    const RemovedBus back = std::move(*m_removedBus);
    m_removedBus.reset();

    // THE IDENTITY IS THE POINT: a restore that minted a new bus number would put
    // back a STRANGER — a slide, a scene or a saved route that names the deleted
    // bus would not find what came back. So the same node ids are reused, and if
    // something else already answers to them this refuses instead of duplicating.
    const std::string audio = back.item.engineId.toStdString();
    const std::string video = back.item.engineIdVideo.toStdString();
    if (graph().HasNode(audio) || graph().HasNode(video)) {
        qWarning() << "BusListModel: cannot put" << back.item.name
                   << "back \u2014 another node holds its identity now";
        return false;
    }

    GraphEdit edit;   // the nodes, their meta, their volume AND their routes: one save
    logIfFailed("AddBus(audio)", graph().AddBus(audio, back.item.name.toStdString(),
                                                 bps::production::BusRole::Custom,
                                                 bps::production::SignalType::Audio));
    logIfFailed("AddBus(video)", graph().AddBus(video, back.item.name.toStdString(),
                                                 bps::production::BusRole::Custom,
                                                 bps::production::SignalType::Video));
    logIfFailed("SetMeta(audio)",
                graph().SetMeta(audio, "uiBusType", back.item.type.toStdString()));
    logIfFailed("SetMeta(video)",
                graph().SetMeta(video, "uiBusType", back.item.type.toStdString()));
    const bps::production::VolumeControl v{ dbFromLevel(back.item.level), back.item.muted,
                                            false, 0.0, 0.0 };
    logIfFailed("SetVolume(audio)", graph().SetVolume(audio, v));
    logIfFailed("SetVolume(video)", graph().SetVolume(video, v));
    // The edges the removal took with it, re-made from the stable source nodes.
    for (const QString &src : std::as_const(back.audioSources)) {
        const std::string node = src.toStdString();
        if (graph().HasNode(node))
            logIfFailed("Connect(audio)", graph().Connect(node, audio,
                                                          bps::production::SignalType::Audio));
    }
    for (const QString &src : std::as_const(back.videoSources)) {
        const std::string node = src.toStdString();
        // A video plane takes one provider: a source that has since been routed to
        // this bus's replacement, or a bus that has become audio-only, is skipped
        // rather than forced — the bus still comes back, just not that route.
        if (!graph().HasNode(node) || !graph().CanConnect(node, video,
                                                          bps::production::SignalType::Video))
            continue;
        logIfFailed("Connect(video)", graph().Connect(node, video,
                                                      bps::production::SignalType::Video));
    }

    const int row = std::clamp(back.row, 0, int(m_buses.size()));
    beginInsertRows(QModelIndex(), row, row);
    m_buses.insert(row, back.item);

{

        return;

// The deferral-time repair (see the header): while any bus's cache and the
// graph disagree about how many routes that bus has, re-pull. Counted, not
// compared row by row: both sides come from the same translation, so the case
// this exists for is a cache built before the rosters had rows (every edge
// translating to "no such row": 0 against the graph's N). A roster ROW SHIFT
// keeps the counts and is already covered by the roster's own structural
// signals (watchRosters), which is why this does not drag every bus through a
// full re-pull on every tick.
void BusListModel::logBoardState() const
{
    for (int row = 0; row < m_buses.size(); ++row) {
        const BusItem &item = m_buses[row];
        // Level and per-side trims are on the line because they are the OTHER
        // reason a bus card's L/R pair can sit dark: the pair reads the bus's
        // POST-FADER mix, so a bus at volume 0 (where buses are created) is flat
        // however healthy its routes are. "Not glowing" and "not connected" then
        // look identical from outside, and only the numbers tell them apart.
        qInfo().noquote()
            << QStringLiteral("BusListModel: bus %1 \u201C%2\u201D (%3) routes audio %4 video %5 "
                              "level %6 muted %7 gains %8/%9")
                   .arg(QString::number(row), item.name, item.type,
                        QString::number(item.routedAudioInputs.size()),
                        QString::number(item.routedVideoSources.size()),
                        QString::number(item.level, 'f', 1),
                        item.muted ? QStringLiteral("yes") : QStringLiteral("no"),
                        QString::number(item.channelGains.value(0, 1.0), 'f', 2),
                        QString::number(item.channelGains.value(1, 1.0), 'f', 2));
    }
}

void BusListModel::refreshRoutesIfStale()
{
    if (!m_active || m_buses.isEmpty())
        return;
    for (const BusItem &item : m_buses) {
        if (audioRoutesFromGraph(item.engineId.toStdString()).size()
                != item.routedAudioInputs.size()
            || videoRoutesFromGraph(item.engineIdVideo.toStdString()).size()
                != item.routedVideoSources.size()) {
            qInfo() << "BusListModel: re-pulling routes — the cached rows disagreed with the graph"
                    << "(a roster that reported after this board was built)";
            refreshRoutes();
            return;
        }
    }
}

// Full re-sync from the graph — rows added/removed/renamed behind our back.
void BusListModel::refresh()
{
    if (!m_active)
        return;
    beginResetModel();
    m_buses.clear();
    rebuildFromGraph();
    endResetModel();
    // A document that just (re)arrived is held to the running rules in the same
    // session, not on the next launch: an older graph can carry two video
    // providers on one bus or an "asrc:"/"vsrc:" node its roster no longer
    // lists, and until this, only the constructor's deferred sweep ever looked —
    // so a doc restored late kept the extra route (and its line) all session.
    // Both calls are cheap no-ops on a clean graph, and each guards its own
    // readiness (a roster that has not reported is not "empty", it is unknown).
    pruneOrphanSourceEdges();
    trimExtraVideoProviders();
}

```cpp
                           const rendering::Size& size, int busNumber) {
```

// to an output, and this is what makes the wire a picture instead of a note.
//
// It is deliberately NOT BuildBusFeedScene (one full-frame layer): a template
// bus's whole point is its layout. Nor is it BuildSlideScene (which composes
// CONTENT — text bound to a slide, family gates, a style's template): a template
// bus carries no slide content, and its windows are its own.
//
// The windows are refreshed on EVERY call, cache hit included — the geometry is
// the scene's, the pixels are the feeds' (see BusPlane), so a window that stops
// producing frames goes blank rather than freezing on its last picture.
Result<std::string> SceneBuilder::BuildTemplateBusScene(int busNumber,
                                                        const std::vector<ContentBlock>& blocks,
                                                        const std::string& background,
                                                        rendering::RenderEngine& engine,
                                                        rendering::Size size) {
    if (busNumber <= 0)
        return Error::Make(Err::InvalidArgument, "SceneBuilder",
                           "a template bus scene needs the bus's own number");

    const int sw = static_cast<int>(size.width);
    const int sh = static_cast<int>(size.height);
    // The id carries BOTH the bus and the size, like the bus-feed scene: a
    // resolution edit re-keys, and two outputs never share one template picture.
    const std::string sceneId = std::format("tplbus:{}@{}x{}", busNumber, sw, sh);
    if (!engine.GetScene(sceneId).ok()) {
        auto scene = engine.CreateScene(sceneId, std::format("Template bus {}", busNumber), size);
        if (!scene.ok())
            return scene.error();
        (void)engine.AddLayer(sceneId, rendering::Layer("bg", "Background",
                                                        rendering::LayerKind::Background, 0));
        (void)engine.AddLayer(sceneId, rendering::Layer("media", "Media",
                                                        rendering::LayerKind::Video, 1));
        (void)engine.AddLayer(sceneId, rendering::Layer("text", "Text",
                                                        rendering::LayerKind::Text, 2));
        // The template's own background: named = painted, ""/transparent = a
        // keyable frame (the same reading ComposeSlide gives a style's colour).
        if (!background.empty() && background != "transparent") {
            auto bgObj = std::make_shared<rendering::BackgroundObject>(
                "bg", "Background", StyleBuilder::ParseColor(background));
            bgObj->SetBounds(rendering::Rect(0, 0, size.width, size.height));
            bgObj->SetLayer("bg");
            (void)engine.AddObject(sceneId, bgObj, "bg");
        } else {
            scene.value()->SetTransparentBackground(true);
        }
        // The design's own content (text, bands, images) — the same block pass
        // every design renders through — and then the windows' geometry. A `bus`
        // block paints no text, so AddStageBlocks skips it and
        // RecordTemplateWindows owns it: one block, one owner.
        (void)AddStageBlocks(engine, sceneId, blocks, size, "tpw", "text");
        RecordTemplateWindows(sceneId, blocks, size, busNumber);
        Logger::Instance().Debug(
            std::format("Template bus scene built: {} ({} block(s))", sceneId, blocks.size()),
            "SceneBuilder");
    }
    RefreshBusPlanes(engine, sceneId);
    return sceneId;
}

Template buses: spec
1. What we are building
A new bus kind, template bus. It is created by picking a template, the one already designed in the Edit canvas’s template tab. Its windows are the bus items placed on that template. A template bus accepts several video inputs and one audio input. Once created, it is an ordinary bus: it appears on the Routing page and can be wired to outputs like any other bus.

Existing buses do not change. A normal video bus still takes one video input and a normal audio bus still takes one audio input.

2. Terms
Template: a design made in the Edit canvas’s template tab. It holds media items, text, and bus items, each placed at a position.
Window: a bus item placed on a template. It is a rectangle in the design that shows a live video feed.
Bus (existing): a normal bus that takes one video input and one audio input.
Template bus (new): a bus created from a template. It takes several video inputs and one audio input.
Output: a destination on the Routing page (HDMI screen, NDI, recording, and so on). It takes a video bus and an audio bus.
3. User flow
Design the template. In Edit, open the template tab. Add items, including bus items, and position them. Each bus item is a window.
Create the template bus. In the bus picker, choose the Template category. Pick a template from the list. A new template bus appears, already knowing its windows from the template.

## What changed

Both flags are applied **on top of** the style's own gates — for the active output's spec and for every per-output pass — so a row can close what its theme offers but never open what the theme forbids.

## Status: complete

**Window assignment (independent per window).** Each bus item on a design names its own bus in its meta, chosen from the window's bus picker in the Edit canvas ([EditScreen.qml:1434](qml/screens/edit/EditScreen.qml#L1434)). The engine paints each window's plane from that block's own id ([SceneBuilder.cpp:1441](src/PresentationEngine/modules/presentation/SceneBuilder.cpp#L1441)), so several windows on one design show different buses, independently.

**Output decides direct vs compose.** `videoMode` lives on the output row, persists only when non-default ([OutputStore.cpp:83](src/PresentationEngine/modules/project/OutputStore.cpp#L83)), and drives the spec at [OutputListModel.cpp:1495](qml/models/OutputListModel.cpp#L1495):
- **compose** → gate open, every window paints its own assigned bus inside its rectangle, design composed by the scene builder;
- **direct** → gate closed with an empty allow-list (windows skipped, not blanked), and the routed bus fills the frame by itself.

The program pass always paints no window ([OutputListModel.cpp:1447](qml/models/OutputListModel.cpp#L1447)), so an output with no wire never inherits the active row's picture. Toggling re-pushes the spec immediately, so the change lands next tick.

The gap I closed this turn: the switch existed only on sink cards. HDMI screen cards now have it too ([RoutingScreen.qml:525](qml/screens/settings/RoutingScreen.qml#L525)) — that was the missing half for the common case.

**Gate chips.** Overlays and Media are now connector-style nodes on every output card — dot, stub of line, initial `O`/`M` ([RoutingNodeCard.qml](qml/components/RoutingNodeCard.qml)) — lit when open, hollow and muted when closed. They sit on the subtitle line so they can't collide with a sink's status and transport pills, they're not ports (no drag, no canvas hit-test), and one press flips that row's flag via [toggleCardGate](qml/screens/settings/RoutingScreen.qml#L1845).                                                    rendering::Size size) {
    if (busId <= 0)
        return Error::Make(Err::InvalidArgument, "SceneBuilder",
                           "a bus feed needs the bus's own number");

    const int sw = static_cast<int>(size.width);
    const int sh = static_cast<int>(size.height);
    // The id carries BOTH the bus and the size (see the header): an output at
    // 720p and one at 4K never share a scene, and a resolution edit re-keys.
    const std::string sceneId = std::format("busfeed:{}@{}x{}", busId, sw, sh);
    if (!engine.GetScene(sceneId).ok()) {
        auto scene = engine.CreateScene(sceneId, std::format("Bus {}", busId), size);
        if (!scene.ok())
            return scene.error();
        // The video layer the picture is painted on ("media" — the layer the
        // compositor's own live layers use), declared once with the scene.
        (void)engine.AddLayer(sceneId, rendering::Layer("media", "Bus feed",
                                                        rendering::LayerKind::Video, 1));

## The compile break

`BusListModel.cpp` had the 4-argument `createBusRow` while the header still declared 5 — your build ran in the window between my two edits, so it caught the mismatch, not a real defect. Both sides agree now, and it's a single 5-arg declaration with the default id.

The Template type is back, and the template picker is **one dropdown** (the app's own `SelectField`, the same control every Settings picker uses — not a Controls ComboBox, which this dialog has no import for):

- Options come from the **Buses category** of the template library ([busTemplates](qml/screens/settings/AudioVideoScreen.qml#L1086)).

- **Audio & Video lists bus templates** — a read-only `BUS TEMPLATES` section under the bus roster, in the same row rhythm, each row showing its name and window count, plus the empty-state telling you to make one in Edit · Templates → Buses ([AudioVideoScreen.qml:2199](qml/screens/settings/AudioVideoScreen.qml#L2199)). Template buses: spec
1. What we are building
A new bus kind, template bus. It is created by picking a template, the one already designed in the Edit canvas’s template tab. Its windows are the bus items placed on that template. A template bus accepts several video inputs and one audio input. Once created, it is an ordinary bus: it appears on the Routing page and can be wired to outputs like any other bus.

Existing buses do not change. A normal video bus still takes one video input and a normal audio bus still takes one audio input.

2. Terms
Template: a design made in the Edit canvas’s template tab. It holds media items, text, and bus items, each placed at a position.
Window: a bus item placed on a template. It is a rectangle in the design that shows a live video feed.
Bus (existing): a normal bus that takes one video input and one audio input.
Template bus (new): a bus created from a template. It takes several video inputs and one audio input.
Output: a destination on the Routing page (HDMI screen, NDI, recording, and so on). It takes a video bus and an audio bus.
3. User flow
Design the template. In Edit, open the template tab. Add items, including bus items, and position them. Each bus item is a window.
Create the template bus. In the bus picker, choose the Template category. Pick a template from the list. A new template bus appears, already knowing its windows from the template.
Route video into it. On the Routing page, drag camera or media sources onto the template bus’s video port. Several can go in.
Route audio into it. Drag one audio source onto its audio port.
Wire it to an output. Drag the template bus’s video port to an output’s video port, and its audio port to the output’s audio port. This works exactly as it does for a normal bus.
On air. The output shows the template’s design, with each window filled by its video feed.
4. Data model
4.1 Bus kind
A bus has a type field. Add a new value, "template".
A template bus stores the id of the template it was created from, in a new meta key templateId.
Windows are not stored on the bus. They are read from the template at render time. This means editing the template updates the bus automatically.
4.2 Windows
A window is a design block of kind bus on the template.
The existing busId meta on a bus block means “this block shows that normal bus”. A window on a template bus does not use busId. It needs its own stable identifier, which is the block’s id within the template. Open: confirm that block ids in the template are stable across edits. If they are not, a new stable window id is needed.
4.3 Routing (graph)
Video edges into a template bus are many-to-one. There is no capacity limit.
Audio edges into a template bus: one only. The second audio edge is refused.
A template bus has one video output side and one audio output side, the same as a normal bus.
Outputs keep their current videoBusId and audioBusId. A template bus fills those slots like any other bus.
5. Rendering
A template bus produces one video frame per tick. That frame is the template design, with each window replaced by its assigned video feed.
The design is composed by the existing scene builder. Windows are painted by the existing bus-plane code, with the source of each plane changed from “a normal bus” to “the feed assigned to this window”.
The audio of a template bus is the single audio input, routed through the normal audio mixer.
Cache keys must include the template id and the set of assigned feeds, so that changing a feed invalidates the cached scene.
6. Required UI
Bus picker (BusSourceModal): add a “Template” category. It lists templates from the template library. Picking one creates a template bus.
Routing page: the template bus is a bus card. Its subtitle shows Template · N in, where N is the number of video inputs. Its video port accepts many wires. Its audio port accepts one.
Edit canvas: no change.
Audio & Video page: no new column. Template buses are created from the bus picker, as the spec above describes.
7. Open questions (must be answered before build)
Which window does each camera fill? Options:
a) You choose a window for each camera when you route it.
b) Cameras fill windows in the order they were routed.
c) Each window has a fixed name, and cameras are matched to names.
What does an empty window show? Options: the design background, blank, or a placeholder.
What happens when the template changes after a template bus is created?
a) Windows added: do they get a slot with no feed? Routing sees the new slot.
b) Windows removed: what happens to the feed that was in them? Is it dropped, or moved?
What happens when a template is deleted while a template bus uses it? Options: refuse the delete, or detach the bus and show a warning.
Audio with several windows. Audio is one input for the whole bus. Does that audio belong to every window, or only to the bus as a whole?
Clean output. Do we still need a “full-frame feed” option that shows one window full-screen? If so, which window?
8. Non-goals
No change to normal buses.
No change to the Edit canvas beyond reading bus items.
No A&V template column.
No HTML output work.
No change to how outputs store their audio.
9. Acceptance tests

Route three video sources into the template bus. All three are accepted. Route a fourth: it is accepted and the rule in open question 1 decides where it goes.
Route two audio sources into the template bus. The second is refused.
Wire the template bus to an output. The output’s frame shows the template design, with each window filled.
Edit the template: move a window. The output updates without recreating the bus.
Delete a source that feeds a window. That window shows its empty state.
Existing normal buses still accept one video input, and their outputs still show the clean full-frame feed.
10. Build and checks
Build and run the app with the repo’s dev cycle script, as AGENTS.md describes.
Run the three repo guards: the lock-scope guard, the interface-thread guard, and the settings-keys guard.
Report unbuilt or untested parts honestly. Do not claim a feature works until it has been run.

**What I found on disk.** The picker tile's corner light had been reduced to a fixed colour for any source no bus carries:

```qml
readonly property color lightColor: root.creating && !busTile.alreadyFed
    ? Theme.dangerLight          // <- every unrouted card, whatever the device is doing
    : monitor.statusColor
```

That is exactly "the probe is not working": `BusMonitor.status` still ran, but its answer was thrown away for the cards in the New Bus picker, so a dead camera, a closed window and a perfectly good camera all painted the same colour. The `lightState` hook had the same hole (it returned the literal `"unrouted"`), so nothing could catch it either.

**The change, in [BusSourceModal.qml](qml/components/BusSourceModal.qml):** the colour is now always the probe's own answer — `monitor.statusColor` (green connected · amber offline/starved · red no device), never a substitute. What separates "connected" from "not routed" is the **form**, not the colour:

- a source a bus already carries → the **filled** dot, the connection light from Media › Inputs;
- a source no bus carries → a **hollow ring** in that same probe colour.

So a camera whose window is closed is an amber ring, an unplugged one is red, a fine-but-unrouted one is a green ring — readable as "device state" while never claiming a connection it does not have. `lightState` now returns the probe's word unchanged, and a new `lightRouted` carries the form half.

**The test that should have caught it** — `newBusCheckLights` in [Main.qml](qml/Main.qml#L2965) — compared the light against a *made-up* `"unrouted"` expectation, which is why a flat colour passed its own scenario. It now checks both halves: `lightState` must equal the probe (`inputAvailable` / `inputDelivery`, `"none"` for a row with no label) **and** `lightRouted` must equal whether a bus carries the row. A card painting one flat colour fails on either count.

+QString OutputListModel::nextStableId() const
+{
+    // "out-<n>", one past every id this roster holds. PARSED, never counted:
+    // rows get reordered and deleted, so a max-suffix scan is the only answer
+    // that cannot hand out a live id — and two rows sharing one id would share

+            continue;
+        bool ok = false;
+        const qulonglong n = item.id.mid(4).toULongLong(&ok);
+        if (ok && n > highest)
+            highest = n;
+    }
+    return QStringLiteral("out-%1").arg(highest + 1);
+}
